journal.harmontide.guide.market.title: Market Day
journal.harmontide.guide.market: Every 6 days (the 4th, 10th, 16th and 22nd of the 24), if you are home that morning, a travelling girl from a family that doesn't live at your hearth sets up beside it, most often a kind you have never met. Hand her an emerald for a bundle of her country's finds; she has four to sell. She moves on the next day, unless you have made a friend of her. Once your hearth is a village, set a market stall within 16 blocks of it (a red and white awning over sticks, planks and a chest). Every morning the passing trade buys half of what's on it, four items to the emerald, and each resident lays out something new: a farmhand her crops, a cook her baking, a guard arrows, anyone else the kind of present she'd bring you. Out on the plains and meadows stand wayside inns, kept by a holstaur. Every morning a traveller or two from far away stops over for the day: make a friend of one and she stays. An emerald to the innkeeper buys a hot meal, and sometimes a map a traveller left behind. (/harmontide locate inn)
journal.harmontide.guide.rivals.title: Rivals
journal.harmontide.guide.rivals: Some wild kinds can't stand each other, by their branch of the tree of life rather than their looks: cats, hyenas and mongooses with rodents, snakes with rodents and frogs, wolves and foxes with hares and rodents, spiders, bats and frogs with insects, seals and bears with fish, and the mongoose and meerkat with snakes. When they meet, one glowers and the other runs. Nobody gets hurt, and once a girl is your friend she has better things to do.
message.harmontide.role.chosen: %s has grown up and wants to be a %s.
journal.harmontide.guide.roles.title: Callings
journal.harmontide.guide.roles: A daughter who grows up picks a calling from what she grew up around. Farmland makes a farmhand: crops grow faster where she tends them. A kitchen (furnace, smoker, campfire or fridge) makes a cook: now and then she cooks something raw in a fridge. A bell or an iron golem makes a guard, tougher and stronger. Otherwise she becomes a scout: her expeditions take half the time and bring more home. A grown daughter may take a shine to a villager (or give the villager a flower while she is near to introduce them). After three mornings near each other they are wed, and now and then a little one comes along: your grandchild, as devoted to you as her mother is. Two at most each. Toys tip the scales, one a day: a wooden hoe for a farmhand, a bowl for a cook, a wooden sword for a guard, a compass for a scout. Show a little one a written book to read it to all the little ones near.
journal.harmontide.guide.teamwork.title: Teamwork
journal.harmontide.guide.teamwork: Two friends fighting the same foe set each other up: a blow within three seconds of a teammate's lands half again as hard. A harpy knocks the foe into the air, and a slime or spider girl slows it down.
advancement.harmontide.teamwork.desc: Have two of your friends land a combined blow

advancement.harmontide.naturalist.desc: Fully study 25 kinds in your journal
journal.harmontide.guide.bestiary.title: Watching
journal.harmontide.guide.bestiary: A kind you have only glimpsed gets just her name here. Watch her kind a while and her home and her moment fill in; watch longer, or befriend one, and you learn her ways. Fully study 25 kinds to be a naturalist. A spyglass helps: whoever is in its crosshair, up to 64 blocks off, is studied twice as fast.
message.harmontide.birthday.thanks: %s is delighted you remembered her birthday!
advancement.harmontide.birthday.desc: Bring a friend something to eat on her birthday
journal.harmontide.guide.treats.title: Treats and Birthdays
journal.harmontide.guide.treats: Every girl has a favourite treat from her homeland. She takes it even if it isn't what she usually eats, and it means three times as much. And every girl has a birthday on one of the 24 days of the calendar: bring a friend something to eat that day and she'll never forget it. Look at a friend to see her birthday. A girl who is expecting craves one food and tells you when you come near; bring it to her before her time and she has twins. On her birthday, light a candle on a cake near her: she comes to blow it out, and everyone there is the closer for her wish.

journal.harmontide.guide.games.title: Games
journal.harmontide.guide.games: Crouch and touch a friend with an empty hand to play hide and seek: count to ten while she hides, then find her within three minutes. Daughters love it most. Hit a friend with a snowball and she'll throw them right back for a while. Show a friend a banner while pointing at somewhere a little way off and she'll race you there (win, and she pays up). Hand her a shovel and she'll bury one of her presents nearby under suspicious sand or gravel: she calls warmer and colder as you look, and a brush digs it out. Crouch and show a friend a bow near a target block for an archery match: three arrows each, closer to the middle scores more.

journal.harmontide.guide.mining.title: Mining Trips
journal.harmontide.guide.mining: Diggers (dwarves, gnomes, kobolds, moles, ants, constructs and more; look for "Miner") will mine for you. Hand one a pickaxe, then show her what to look for: an ore, raw metal, an ingot, a gem, coal or stone. She digs in at her patrol spot (or where she stands) and comes back there with a stack, into a chest beside the spot or into your hands. Rare things take days and wear the pickaxe; Efficiency, Fortune and Unbreaking help. Crouch with an empty hand to take your pickaxe back. She leaves a laddered shaft beside the spot that goes deeper while she's down (natural ground only), and brings up any ore she struck on the way.
message.harmontide.salami: %s eats the salami and longs for you (%s%%)
message.harmontide.foraging.off: %s goes out to gather %s. She'll be back in about %s minutes.
message.harmontide.foraging.waiting: %s is back from foraging and waits at %s %s %s until you come by
journal.harmontide.guide.foraging.title: Foraging
journal.harmontide.guide.foraging: Gatherers (plants, rabbits, rodents, foxes, bugs, marsupials and centaurs; look for "Forager") will forage for you. Crouch and show one something that grows wild: berries, mushrooms, tar-shrooms, apples, flowers, saplings, seeds, honeycomb. She goes out and comes back to her patrol spot (or where she stood) with sixteen of it and your sample, into a chest beside the spot or into your hands. Berries take a few hours, rare seeds days.
journal.harmontide.guide.longing.title: Longing
journal.harmontide.guide.longing: Close friends miss you when you are away, and longing adds to it even while you are near. Tar-shrooms (black mushrooms of swamps and dark forests; they spread in the dark) make grown friends nearby long for you a little at a time, and a salami fed to one makes her long a lot. Leave for a minute or more and come back: if she misses you, she cuddles up to you, and is more likely to come to bed and to have young that day.
message.harmontide.stargazing.join: %s comes and sits down beside you to watch the stars
message.harmontide.stargazing.wish: A shooting star! %s makes a wish, and whispers it to you: a never-ending pile of %s
message.harmontide.stargazing.star: A shooting star! Your friends make their wishes
message.harmontide.stargazing.alone: A shooting star streaks across the sky
journal.harmontide.guide.stargazing: On a clear night, stand still under open sky and look up at the stars. After a while your friends nearby come and sit beside you to look up. Before long a shooting star crosses the sky (one a night): everyone beside you grows a little closer, and one of them whispers her wish, which tells you her favourite treat. Each star falls through a constellation you haven't seen yet: the journal's cover keeps count of all twelve. Now and then, on a clear night in cold country, the sky fills with an aurora. A frost-touched girl or two comes out under it (and goes at dawn, unless she's made a friend), and aurora shards fall to the snow: every girl loves to be given one.

message.harmontide.favour.done: %s is so glad of it, and presses a few emeralds into your hand
journal.harmontide.guide.favours.title: Favours
journal.harmontide.guide.favours: Now and then a grown friend near you asks you for something she needs: candles, string, paper, ingots, whatever her people use. Look at her to see what (it shows on her info). Bring it within three days, all at once or a few at a time, and hand it to her: she is glad of it, grows closer, and gives you a few emeralds. You only owe one favour at a time.
message.harmontide.story: By the fire, %s tells a story of the %s (%s). You note it in your journal
message.harmontide.story.old: By the fire, %s tells an old story you have heard before, and tells it well
journal.harmontide.guide.stories.title: Stories by the fire
journal.harmontide.guide.stories: At night, sit by a lit campfire with two or more friends around it. One of them will tell a story (one a night), most often of a kind of her own branch of the tree of life that you haven't met, else one from her own people: its page opens in your journal, with where it lives. Everyone listening grows a little closer.

journal.harmontide.guide.colds.title: Colds
journal.harmontide.guide.colds: Leave a girl out in the rain or snow somewhere cold for a few minutes and she may catch a cold (sea folk, the undead, constructs and slimes never do). She sneezes and is a little slow for three days. Hand her mushroom stew, beetroot soup, rabbit stew or a honey bottle and she feels better at once, and is grateful to whoever looked after her.

journal.harmontide.guide.visits.title: Daily visits
journal.harmontide.guide.visits: Friends notice when you come by. The first time each day you are near one, she is glad to see you (a little closer), and counts the days in a row. Every week without a day missed she tells you so and grows closer still. Her info shows the count.

journal.harmontide.guide.watch.title: Keeping watch
journal.harmontide.guide.watch: A friend on patrol keeps watch at night: when you are away and a monster comes near her post, she calls out to you with where it is. If a grown friend dies, a poppy with her name falls where she did, and your journal's cover remembers her.

journal.harmontide.guest: A guest here: her true kin are few, so she lives with her nearest relatives

journal.harmontide.guide.tree.title: The tree of life
journal.harmontide.guide.tree: Every kind belongs to a branch of the tree of life: cats with hyenas and mongooses, whales with hippos, salamanders with frogs. A body can fool you (the hyena runs like a dog), her branch decides her milk. The pages after the guide keep count of each branch you have started; meet every kind on one branch to complete it and earn its charm (in your offhand it lends that branch's milk's first effect). Your first friend of a kind gets talked about: wild ones of her branch nearby start a little fond of you. When a branch is down to its last kind or two, a 'Still to meet' page tells you where they live (but not who they are).

journal.harmontide.guide.rain.title: Sun and rain
journal.harmontide.guide.rain: Cats of every kind hate getting wet: caught in the rain with nowhere to be, a feliform looks for a roof nearby and waits it out. Frogs, newts and salamanders love it, and a friend of theirs who stands out in the rain with them grows a little closer (once a shower). Friends warn you a minute before it starts. Snakes, lizards, turtles and crocodiles are cold-blooded: on a clear morning they lie in the sun for a while and get up warmed through, and a friend who keeps them company there is a little closer.
message.harmontide.basking: %s stretches out in the sun beside you
message.harmontide.moon_howl: %s howls at the full moon, and you feel it in your bones
journal.harmontide.guide.habits.title: Habits
journal.harmontide.guide.habits: Each branch has its habits. Wolves, dogs and foxes howl at the full moon, and every canid in earshot answers; stand under the moon with a friend among them and you are closer for it. Monkeys and apes groom a friend beside them, picking out poison, hunger or the like now and then. Elephants and their kin spray a burning friend out. Walk beside a hoofed friend (cattle, goats, deer, camels, horses) and you find your footing the way she does, stepping up whole blocks without a jump. Bears, raccoons and their furry kin wrap up a friend who is freezing. Crabs, lobsters and shrimp comb the beach: stand on the sand by the water and one digs up something at your feet now and then. Fairies, pixies and the leshy leave fairy rings of mushrooms on the grass at night; stand in one (any ring of mushrooms will do) and you are lucky till morning. Hares and rabbits hear trouble first: one thumps the ground when a monster comes, and you learn what it is and which way. Fall beside a slime friend and you land on her, softly. With one of the made folk beside you, an anvil you work never wears down.

journal.harmontide.guide.nesting.title: Nesting boxes
journal.harmontide.guide.nesting: Build a nesting box (planks around a bit of wheat) and set it down where your hens are. Any egg laid within four blocks of it, by a chicken or a harpy, goes into the hay instead of rolling about. Take the eggs out with an empty hand, or let a hopper do it; a friend on patrol nearby empties it into the fridge. Up on the peaks, the windswept hills and the stony shores harpies keep aeries: crags topped with nests, one kind to a colony, led by a matriarch. Befriend her and the colony takes you in. At home, a harpy perch (a hay bale and two feathers on spruce) draws a passing flock to settle round it for good. (/harmontide locate aerie)

journal.harmontide.guide.orders.title: Orders and getting around
journal.harmontide.guide.orders: A stick gives a friend her orders: sit, patrol, follow or roam; sneak with it for her stance. Sneak with the whistle and everyone near stays put; do it again and they all follow you. Followers go through portals with you, take the free seat in your boat, and wait where they are while you are away. Sneak with the friend compass and the friends near you glow. Your arrows and blasts pass them by, and you hear it when one is badly hurt. The command /harmontide friends lists them all, wherever they are.

journal.harmontide.guide.realm.title: The Demon Realm
journal.harmontide.guide.realm: Deep in some dark forests and swamps (where a little shrine of black stone and purple candles sometimes keeps the realm's gifts), and wherever a wild Lilith lives, the ground turns to purple Demon Realm grass, and it creeps on by itself in the dark, a few steps past where it began, up into the trees, which weep violet sap; pale weepcaps glow among the roots, and the air turns heavy and rose-dark. Friends standing in it blush, miss you more and flirt more often. Its heartfruit bushes bear fruit: a close friend who eats one is lovestruck with you for a few minutes. Animals and monsters that linger on it in the dark change into monster girls of their kind: a witch into a succubus, a cow into a holstaur, an iron golem into a golem, a slime into a slime girl; a tamed pet stays devoted to you. Parrots become macaw harpies and frogs frog girls. Villagers, wandering traders, pigs, cats and chickens are possessed instead: they keep their own shape, but their eyes glow violet and the realm's haze rises from them, and possessed animals seek out one of their own kind every half day, and their young are born piglettes, nekomata or poultry harpies. After a day possessed, the realm takes a pig, cat or chicken altogether the next time she is in the dark: she becomes a piglette, a nekomata or a poultry harpy herself. A possessed villager or wandering trader comes to a sleeping player's bed instead: one who spends the night there has a little succubus or demon a day later, devoted to that player. Give one a heartfruit and she seeks your bed that night from far off (and if she is slow, she slips in through the haze); and she speaks well of her young's father to the village. A possessed cat brings her owner a heartfruit each morning. Possessed animals follow a heartfruit held out to them, and one fed to any possessed creature makes her ready for her own kind at once. At night a possessed villager passes it on to a villager standing close by, so a village slowly turns. Little patches of the realm take root under them, and a golem among three of them turns too. Splash holy water (holy water and gunpowder), thrown, frees every possessed creature where it breaks. A holy font (calcite, holy water and gold) wards twelve blocks round it: the realm can't take hold there and nobody is possessed or turned. Now and then a wandering trader arrives already possessed, with a realm explorer map among her wares. Holy water drives it out of them. A holstaur fills a glass bottle with her milk, which makes you strong; baked into a heartfruit tart with heartfruit, wheat and sugar, it leaves a close friend lovestruck three times as long. Deep in the realm at night a wild succubus or demon sometimes steps out of the haze, and under a full moon the realm spreads fast and its own dance the sabbath. Changed ones still burn with the realm, and slip into any sleeper's bed, friend or not. A succubus near your bed visits your dreams: a close one brings a sweet dream and a lucky morning; a wild one feeds on some of your experience and leaves a heartfruit, unless a tapir guards your sleep. A realm censer (chain, iron, heartfruit and an amethyst shard) fed a heartfruit burns for a day, and the girls within eight blocks of it feel the realm's air without its ground: they flirt and miss you as if they stood in it. A realm log cut down and kept makes dark purple realm planks, stairs, slabs, fences, gates, doors and trapdoors that stay purple in any light. (/harmontide locate realm finds the nearest wild patch.) Realm silver (an iron ingot, four amethyst shards and a heartfruit) makes a sword that cuts the spirit, not the flesh: it wounds no monster girl, but stops her fighting and leaves her blushing and a little fonder of you; anything else it cuts like iron. Realm silver armour guards like iron; two pieces soften a monster girl's blows by half, and a full set keeps wild ones from picking a fight. About one night in ten the moon rises rose-violet: that night the realm stirs, turning creatures twice as fast and spreading, possessing and calling its own four times as often. Torchlight turns it back to grass, and so does holy water (three bottles, a water bucket and a gold nugget). Silk touch takes the grass home. Deep in a few dark forests a Lilith keeps a manor of realm wood with her succubi, a throne, and the realm's treasures in a chest. (/harmontide locate manor) In the badlands stands the Demon's spire: a blackstone tower of four storeys (a hall with succubi on guard, a library, a bedchamber, a treasury) and on its roof, under the open sky, the Demon on her throne. (/harmontide locate spire) The realm takes on the land it spreads into: where it is cold enough to snow it is the frost realm, on mud and in swamps the bog realm (weepcaps thrive there, heartfruit does not), and on sand realm sand (heartfruit, but no weepcaps).

journal.harmontide.guide.season.title: Mating season
journal.harmontide.guide.season: Each branch of the tree of life has three restless days in every forty, each at its own time. A grown friend in season stays close to you, blushes, flirts more and comes to bed more readily. Cold calms her: a cold biome, or a snowball or ice handed to her, which settles her until next season. journal.harmontide.guide.marriage.title: Marriage
journal.harmontide.guide.marriage: A wedding ring (a diamond on three gold ingots) given to a grown friend who adores you, at full friendship, is a proposal. Stand by a hearth together and the wedding is held: your friends nearby gather round. A spouse forgives any absence, comes to bed more readily, and while she is near you have two more hearts (each spouse near adds two more, up to six). Many spouses are one happy family: a wife nearby blesses each new proposal, the wives are bridesmaids, a pat for one warms the others, two or more in your bed make a family bed, and if one is lost the rest hold you close. Guests bring wedding presents, and the first three days are a honeymoon. Wed by a lit realm censer instead and the Demon Realm keeps your vows. Propose at her kind of place (as on a date) and it's perfect. Of a morning, a wife you pass packs you lunch, and one who shared your bed may have dreamt of a real place nearby: go there together. Use a plain painting on your hearth with the family gathered round for a portrait with their names. A girl who adores you may not wait to be asked: after a lovely date she might hand you the ring herself. Every forty days she wears her veil again; give her the ring by a hearth on the day and you renew your vows, with the friends gathered round, the bouquet and a second honeymoon. At the wedding she names a place she has always wanted to see; take her there for a souvenir and a pack of what you found. Before any ring, ask her out: sneak and give a close friend a flower, and she'll tell you her kind of place (lots of flowers, the water's edge, somewhere high with a view, or the open night sky). Take her there and stay together half a minute.

journal.harmontide.guide.order.title: The Order
journal.harmontide.guide.order: The Order is sworn to wipe out the Demon Realm. By day, now and then, a patrol of its sisters (two knights in white and gold, and an inquisitrix in a navy hood) marches on a realm patch near you to purge it: realm grass turns back where they walk, and the inquisitrix blesses all of it around her. They free the possessed with a touch, and they put the realm's own to the sword: devils, and every girl the realm changed. Ordinary girls they leave alone. The Order hears of your ties to the realm: time spent in its air, devils and changed girls among your friends, heartfruit handed out. Once it has heard enough, you are marked: sisters fight you and the friends at your side, and patrols come looking for you. When it has heard far too much, a crusade comes for your hearth one night: a captain under the Order's banner and her band. Beat every one of them and your household is the fonder of you; if any still stand at dawn, they withdraw, and your household is shaken. A realm silver blade cuts a sister's faith, not her flesh, and so does the realm's air in the dark: with no faith left she kneels and lays down her sword. Feed a kneeling sister a heartfruit and she falls to the realm, a succubus (a captain a demon) devoted to you; with an empty hand you spare her, and she goes home. A sister you spared remembers: a couple of days later, while the Order doesn't have you marked, she comes back to your hearth unarmed, as a chaplain, and stays three days. Any wedding or vow renewal at a hearth while she is there gets her blessing. The Order thinks better of mercy and of exorcism. (/harmontide order tells you how the Order sees you.)

journal.harmontide.guide.kindred.title: Kindred of the Realm
journal.harmontide.guide.kindred: Keep company with the Demon Realm long enough and it takes to you. Time in its air, heartfruit you eat, nights beside one of its own, a wife of the realm's own at your side, and sisters of the Order you bring to fall all leave its touch on you. Touched, you see in the realm's dark and its haze rises from you. Kindred, its own know you: wild devils and realm-changed girls let you be unless you strike first, they are a little likelier to share your bed, and you move quickly in its air. The Order counts it against you: a sister who sees you sprinkles holy water on you, and a chaplain won't bless your wedding. Realm-born, the realm feeds you while you stand in its air, its night makes you strong, and you are hardier everywhere (two more hearts). Splash holy water washes much of it out, and time near a holy font a little. (/harmontide realm touch tells you how far it has gone.)

journal.harmontide.guide.family.title: Family
journal.harmontide.guide.family: A girl who is expecting craves one food and tells you; bring it before her time for twins (a harpy lays a full clutch). When her time comes you hear of it wherever you are, and little ones born to you come with a name. A cradle (planks around wool, on two sticks) lets them nap at night and grow twice as fast; rock it for a lullaby. Read them a written book. Give a little one a toy each day: a wooden hoe, a bowl, a wooden sword or a compass tips what she grows up to be. Be near as she grows: her first word, a flower, a drawing. In a thunderstorm she runs to you. Grown, she brings you the first thing of her calling. Use a plain painting on your hearth with the family round you for a portrait. On Reunion Day (the 12th of every 24) your grown children who live away come home at dusk with their sweethearts and little ones, if you are by your hearth, and go back the next morning. A grown daughter who settles at your hearth builds a house of her own a little way off, with a cradle and a bed for her sweetheart, who moves in once they are wed; visit it when it's done. The journal lists them all and draws your family tree, wife by wife and generation by generation, and /harmontide family tells you where everyone is.

journal.harmontide.guide.courtship.title: Old customs
journal.harmontide.guide.courtship: Some kinds take to a stranger in their own way. Fighters (lizard warriors, the old bull breeds, oni and giants, hellhounds and wolves, wyrms, valkyries, dark elves, lionesses) respect whoever beats them face to face: bring one to half health in melee and she yields instead of falling. Arrows don't count. Spinners and the tigress snare someone they fancy and come to claim them: don't strike her, and she claims you. House spirits (kikimora, brownie, domovoi) let themselves in by your hearth while you are home and keep it; after a few visits they stay fond of the house. Each works once per creature, and only before she is fond of you.

By day, while you are home, she walks up to the fire and looks the place over: a bed for each resident there, at least eight food put away in a fridge or chest, nobody hurt, residents fond of you, and no monsters about. Two points each. Six or more pays an emerald a point; ten also makes you a hero of the villages for a day. Under six you only get a warning. Her written report says what to fix.

journal.harmontide.guide.care.title: Care needs
journal.harmontide.guide.care: Some kinds need a little more from the home you share. A merfolk who lives at your hearth needs a pool: six or more blocks of still water within eight of the fire. She lives in it and never dries out at home; without one she reminds you every day, and it sours her a little. Lamias are cold-blooded: in a cold land they slow to a crawl unless warmed by a winter coat, a fire or campfire close by, or a hot spring. Harpies moult every few days and give their favourite a handful of feathers.

journal.harmontide.guide.trials.title: Legendary trials
journal.harmontide.guide.trials: A wild legend tests anyone who comes near before she counts them a friend. The great birds, the deep's giants and the great serpents ask for an offering: hand it to her. Dragons, hellhounds, giants and the riders want to be bested face to face: bring her to half health in melee and she yields. The night's own and the sacred beasts want a vigil: stay close by her from dusk to dawn. A trial lasts three days. Pass it and she is fond of you and gives her relic: the sky plume, tide pearl, serpent's eye, dragon scale or moon mirror, each with its own gift.

journal.harmontide.guide.pacts.title: Spirit pacts
journal.harmontide.guide.pacts: The four elemental spirits bind themselves to one they love. Crouch and hand an amethyst shard to a devoted salamander, undine, sylph or gnome, and her element goes with you everywhere. Fire: your blows set foes alight. Water: water and rain heal you. Wind: you are light on your feet, and quick under the open sky. Earth: deep underground you dig fast and stand firm. One spirit of each element at a time; a shard again ends the pact, and it ends if she dies.

Harpies' feathers make the winged cap, which you craft.

journal.harmontide.guide.merchants.title: Wandering merchants
journal.harmontide.guide.merchants: Now and then a girl you meet in the wild is a wandering merchant, sparkling green over her pack. An empty hand opens her trades: the wares of her branch of the tree of life, milk and wool from the cattle, silk from the spinners, saplings from the flora, realm fruit from the devils, gold from the dragons. She buys bread for the road. Each trade makes her a little fonder of you. After two days she moves on, unless someone has made a friend of her: then she stays.

journal.harmontide.guide.squad: Up to four of your fighting friends can be your squad: crouch and use a goat horn on one to enlist her, and again to let her go. Blow the horn and every squad member within earshot comes running and goes for the monsters around you for two minutes. Whatever strikes you, the squad near you turns on. And when the Order brings a crusade to your hearth, your squad marches home to defend it.
message.harmontide.blessing.growth: Your wife's kind has blessed the home: the crops round your hearth grow faster.
message.harmontide.blessing.herd: Your wife's kind has blessed the home: the animals round your hearth grow up and thrive faster.
message.harmontide.blessing.catch: Your wife's kind has blessed the home: luck follows you near the hearth (the fish bite better).
message.harmontide.blessing.ward: Your wife's kind has blessed the home: monsters that come near your hearth are marked and weakened.
message.harmontide.blessing.hoard: Your wife's kind has blessed the home: your hands work quicker near the hearth.
message.harmontide.blessing.soothe: Your wife's kind has blessed the home: by the hearth your wounds close gently on their own.
journal.harmontide.guide.blessings.title: Wives bless the land
journal.harmontide.guide.blessings: In the old stories a monster girl changes the place she makes her married home. Each wife near your hearth brings it her kind's blessing, and two or three wives of the same blessing make it stronger. Plant folk, fae, birds and the small grazers make the crops round the hearth grow. Hoofed and horned kinds make young animals grow up and parents ready sooner. Sea, river and shore kinds bring you luck at home, so the fish bite better. Hunters, the made, riders and the dead mark and weaken monsters that come close. Dragons, serpents and spinners quicken your hands (Haste). Devils and slimes close your wounds by the fire.
advancement.harmontide.dead_realm_entere: Set foot on the grave grass of the realm of the dead
journal.harmontide.guide.dead_realm: Where a wild lich or koschei makes her home, the ground turns to ashen grave grass and a grey mist hangs over it. It spreads in the dark, under trees and roofs and at night, but the open sun withers it back to its heart by day, and lamplight, holy water and the Order's sisters cleanse it. Zombies and skeletons that linger on it in the dark rise again as undead girls, and deep in it, at night, one of the dead sometimes climbs out of the ground. Undead friends standing on it are at their strongest. Befriend its lich, and it stops growing.
message.harmontide.sabbath.rank.initiate: Word of you has reached the Sabbath. You are its initiate now: witches will no longer turn on you.
message.harmontide.sabbath.rank.adept: The Sabbath counts you an adept. Offer a witch an empty hand and she will open her table to you.
message.harmontide.sabbath.rank.keeper: The Sabbath trusts you with a familiar of your own.
message.harmontide.sabbath.rank.sibling: The Sabbath calls you its sibling. Its title is yours to carry.
message.harmontide.sabbath.familiar: A black cat with knowing eyes pads out of the dark and settles at your feet: your familiar.
journal.harmontide.guide.sabbath.title: The Sabbath
journal.harmontide.guide.sabbath: The witches' Sabbath is the Demon Realm's own coven, and the Order's oldest rival. Whatever the Order holds against you raises your standing with the Sabbath, and so does dancing at the full-moon sabbath, seeing a creature turned by the realm, and being wed by a realm censer. Tithes, mercy to the Order and holy water lower it. As an initiate, witches leave you alone. As an adept, a witch offered an empty hand opens her table: heartfruit, weepcaps, censers, realm grass and brews. A keeper is given a familiar, a black cat whose eyes you share at night; lose her and another comes at the next full moon. And the Sabbath's sibling carries its title after their name.
advancement.harmontide.sabbath_adept.des: Be welcome at a witch's table
advancement.harmontide.sabbath_keeper.de: Be trusted with a familiar of your own
advancement.harmontide.sabbath_sibling.d: Rise as high as the Sabbath goes
message.harmontide.sea_wedding: %s officiates as the sea bishop and blesses your marriage to %s: the sea is yours to breathe now, as long as you are wed.
message.harmontide.mermaid_blood.given: %s presses a small vial into your hand: a drop of her own blood. Mermaid blood, they say, keeps you strong.
message.harmontide.mermaid_blood.drunk: The mermaid blood runs cold, then warm. You feel stronger, for good.
message.harmontide.mermaid_blood.again: Mermaid blood only works once in a life.
advancement.harmontide.sea_wedding.desc: Be wed to a sea bride by the water, with a sea bishop officiating
advancement.harmontide.mermaid_blood.des: Drink the blood a merfolk friend gave you
journal.harmontide.guide.sea.title: Sea weddings
journal.harmontide.guide.sea: Wed a merfolk or mollusk bride by a hearth with water beside it, and if another sea girl stands among the guests she officiates as the sea bishop. Her blessing lets you breathe the water of the sea, the beaches and the rivers and swim like a dolphin, for as long as you are wed. And once in your life a merfolk close friend may give you a vial of her blood when you pet her: drink it for a lasting extra heart.
message.harmontide.ghost.in: %s slips into you with a cold little shiver. The dark goes clear, and the monsters seem to forget you're there.
message.harmontide.ghost.out: %s slips back out beside you, looking pleased with herself.
message.harmontide.ghost.tired: %s has already been inside you today. She needs to gather herself first.
message.harmontide.ghost.prank: Something cold slips into you: %s! You shiver and hiccup.
message.harmontide.ghost.giggle: %s pops back out of you, giggling.
Let a ghost friend slip into you
journal.harmontide.guide.ghosts.title: Ghost possession
journal.harmontide.guide.ghosts: Ghosts (yurei, banshees, poltergeists, lost souls, lloronas) like to be close to the one they love, as close as can be. Crouch and offer a ghost friend an empty hand and she slips into you for a minute: you see in the dark, a faint glow hangs about you, and monsters lose track of you. Each can do it once a day. Wild ghosts sometimes do it at night as a prank, leaving you shivering and hiccuping.
message.harmontide.cooking.masterful: %s cooks it to perfection, and hands it over with a proud little flourish.
message.harmontide.cooking.clumsy: %s cooks it... mostly. There's a lot of smoke.
message.harmontide.cooking.hopeless: Something catches fire. %s hands you a smoking black lump, beaming. Made with love!
message.harmontide.cooking.busy: %s is still cleaning up from last time.
message.harmontide.cooking.ate_burnt: You eat every bite of it. %s looks like she might cry with happiness.
journal.harmontide.guide.cooking.title: Who can't cook
journal.harmontide.guide.cooking: Crouch and hand a friend something raw (meat, fish, a potato) and she cooks it for you, now and then. Every girl has her own touch in the kitchen and it never changes: a masterful cook's dish fills you up and leaves you strong, a good cook's heals a little, and a plain cook's is just dinner. And some can't cook at all: their burnt love food makes you queasy, but eat it anyway while she's near and she'll be over the moon.
message.harmontide.dullahan.pop: %s startles, and her head pops right off and rolls away!
message.harmontide.dullahan.thanks: %s takes her head back and settles it on her neck, very red in the face. Thank you...
journal.harmontide.guide.dullahan.title: A dullahan's head
journal.harmontide.guide.dullahan: A dullahan's head sits on her neck more by habit than anything. Startle her (a blow, a tease that flusters her, a stumble) and it pops off and rolls away. Headless, she stumbles slowly after it. Catch it first and hand it back, and she'll be very grateful. Keep it, and it finds its own way home after a while.
journal.harmontide.repeadead_undead.home: Graveyards and dark ruins at night
journal.harmontide.repeadead_undead.sign: Grave Scream: Seen, she screams: whoever hears it is frozen in place while she clings to them and drinks their life. Befriended, she leaves friendly creatures be and turns the scream and the grip on monsters.
journal.harmontide.living_armor_undead.s: Steel Faith: She takes hits for her friend: befriended, she stands between them and the monsters, and is hard to hurt.
journal.harmontide.cursed_blade_undead.s: Hungry Edge: Her blade drinks from what it cuts: befriended, her blows heal her a little.
...again. Cut again. I like the way you swing me...
...don't put me down. Don't ever put me down...
...I'm yours. Only yours. Soon you'll see me...
...a heartbeat... how long since I held a heartbeat...
...let them strike. I'll take it. I'll take all of it...
...stay inside me a little longer. It's so warm...
...I want to hold you with real arms...
message.harmontide.cursed.step_out.blade: The black blade shudders, and %s steps out of it, her own sword in her hand. She doesn't plan to leave your side.
message.harmontide.cursed.step_out.armor: The breastplate grows warm, then light, and %s steps out of it, armoured head to foot. She bows to you.
advancement.harmontide.cursed_gear.desc: Use cursed gear until its spirit steps out to meet you
Be frozen by a repeadead's scream
journal.harmontide.guide.cursed.title: Cursed gear
journal.harmontide.guide.cursed: Now and then the chests of old places (dungeons, mineshafts, strongholds, temples, mansions, ancient cities) hold cursed gear: a black blade or a living breastplate, each with a spirit in it. They work as well as iron, and they grow fond of whoever uses them: the blade with every kill, the armour with every blow it takes for you and every minute you wear it. They whisper to you as they do. At full fondness the spirit steps out as a girl, devoted to you from the first: the living armour shrugs off blows and goes for whatever hurts you, and the cursed blade's strikes heal her.
journal.harmontide.guide.repeadead.title: The repeadead
journal.harmontide.guide.repeadead: In dark forests, swamps and the deep dark she stands or crouches stock-still, her mourning mask frozen in horror. Walk in front of her and she screams: you can't move while she comes for you and clings on, drinking your life. Hit her while she holds you to break free. Befriended, she leaves friendly creatures be and turns her scream and her grip on the monsters around you.
journal.harmontide.guide.foodweb.title: The food web
journal.harmontide.guide.foodweb: Wild girls feed themselves as their diet says. Hunters bring down the wild animals of their size (rabbits and chickens for the small, sheep, pigs and goats for most, cows for the big ones), eat the meat where it fell and leave the bones and hide. Fishers take fish and squid. Grazers crop the grass and flowers, and where many graze together the turf wears to bare dirt. Scavengers go where something died and eat what was left. Where the land is eaten out they move on, and thinned-out herds come back over time when no hunter is about. Your animals are safe: nothing tame, named, leashed or penned, nothing in a village or near a hearth. Befriended girls are fed by you and don't hunt.
message.harmontide.carcass.blade: You'd need a blade (a sword or an axe) to butcher it.
journal.harmontide.guide.carcasses.title: Carcasses
journal.harmontide.guide.carcasses: A wild animal killed by anything but you (a hunter, a wolf, a monster, a fall) leaves a carcass where it fell, bloodied, with feathers or wool torn loose round it. Scavengers and hungry hunters come to feed on it, and each meal takes meat off the bones. A cow carries the most meat, a pig a little less, a sheep or goat half as much, a chicken or rabbit a mouthful. Use a sword or an axe on it to butcher it: a share of the meat that's left, the hide or wool, and a bone. After a day it starts to rot (flies, and some of the meat comes away rotten); after two only bones are left, and on the third day nothing.
journal.harmontide.guide.rhythms.title: Day and night
journal.harmontide.guide.rhythms: Every kind keeps its own hours. Most are up by day and sleep at night; night kinds sleep through the day. Dawn-and-dusk kinds are up at first and last light and rest through midday and the dead of night, and a few nap in short bouts round the clock. A wild girl out in the open looks for somewhere covered to sleep first: under trees, an overhang or a roof. Asleep she isn't foraging or watching for you, so that is the time to meet the shy ones. Look at any girl to see her place in the food web and her hours.
journal.harmontide.guide.herds.title: Herds and schools
journal.harmontide.guide.herds: Wild grazers keep together with their own kind, and wild fish-eaters swim together as a school, all heading the same way; a straggler hurries back. Each of them keeps watch. At a monster, a wild hunter of another kind, or a stranger running up (or walking right up), the first to see it calls the alarm. A big herd, or a herd of big kinds, bunches up and faces the danger, hard to hurt; a small one flees together, all the same way. Schools always flee. Sneak, and you can get close.
journal.harmontide.guide.pasture.title: Pastures
journal.harmontide.guide.pasture: The land remembers where it was grazed. A herd of three or more that keeps walking the same ground treads the grass into a game trail; follow one and it leads to them. Where grazers crowd together the turf wears to bare dirt. Once the herd has moved on, the land rests: cropped grass grows back within half a day (now and then a flower with it), bare dirt greens over in a day, and a trail fades back to grass in two.
journal.harmontide.guide.territories: Wild hunters each hold a home range of their own. Now and then one patrols out to its edge and leaves a scent mark there. A rival of her kind who comes across a fresh mark turns away and makes her home somewhere else, so hunters spread out across the land instead of crowding together. You can't smell the marks yourself, but a befriended dog, cat, bear or snake kind can: with one near you, the marks round about show as faint wisps in the colour of whoever left them. Marks fade after two days unless they are renewed.
journal.harmontide.guide.pollination: Bees, moths, butterflies, fairies, pixies and nectar bats go from flower to flower, wild or befriended, and carry pollen between them. A flower they pollinate seeds another of its kind beside it, and the crops, stems and berry bushes round it grow on a little: keep a pollinator friend near your garden. Wild girls who eat fruit, nuts and seeds carry a seed away from their meals and leave it far off on open grass: a sapling suited to the land, or a berry bush in the taiga. They never sow in villages or near a hearth.
journal.harmontide.guide.partners.title: Partnerships
journal.harmontide.guide.partners: Some kinds do better together. Small crabs and shrimp groom the big sea girls (orcas, sharks, krakens) in the water, soothing them and earning a meal. A hermit crab shelters by a sea anemone and is hard to hurt there. Small rodents and rabbit kinds ride close by the big grazers (elephants, giraffes, rhinos), picking them clean and staying safe by them. Ants guard plant girls and go for any monster that comes near them, and pollinators at a plant girl's blossoms keep her thriving. Scavengers trail wild hunters at a distance to be near the kill, and grazers of different kinds heed each other's alarm calls. Partners work for you too: keep an ant friend by your alraune.
journal.harmontide.guide.decomposers: Slimes, the fungus kinds (matango, shiitake, censhroom, shroomotaur, cordyceps) and the date beetle break down whatever is left lying about: rotten flesh, bones, spoiled food, leaves, saplings, seeds and flowers. They pick carcasses to the bone faster and break the last bones into bone meal. What they take in goes back to the soil: coarse dirt loosens, bare dirt greens over, crops and saplings round them get a dose of bone meal. Keep a decomposer friend by your composter and she fills it for you.
journal.harmontide.guide.habitats.title: Microhabitats
journal.harmontide.guide.habitats: Every kind cares about the little things about where she is: shade or sun, water close by or dry ground, heights, caves, cold or heat. Look at a girl to see what she likes and how she feels where she is. Content, she heals slowly and sparkles now and then; ill at ease, she sighs, and a wild one wanders off to find a spot that suits her better. They turn up most where the land suits them, so if you are looking for one, look where she would be comfortable. Make a friend comfortable at home and she will thank you for it with her health.
advancement.harmontide.master_tracker.de: Read the tracks of ten different kinds
journal.harmontide.guide.tracks.title: Tracks and signs
journal.harmontide.guide.tracks: Wild girls leave signs of where they have been. In sand, snow and mud they leave footprints, pointing the way they went: hooves, paws, three-toed claws, bare feet, or the long sweep of a tail. Use an empty hand on footprints to read them: whose they are, how fresh, and which way she went. Every kind you read goes into your field notes. Footprints fade after a day. Bird kinds drop a feather now and then, and the gnawers and antlered kinds strip the bark off logs where nobody took an axe.
journal.harmontide.guide.weather.title: Weather ways
journal.harmontide.guide.weather: Every kind meets the weather in her own way. In a thunderstorm most take cover under trees, an overhang or a roof and huddle there till it passes; the raiju, the sylph and the dragons are thrilled by it instead, faster and stronger in the open. Frogs and newts, slimes, snails and the fungus kinds come out and liven up in the rain, even the ones who usually sleep through the day. When the sun comes back after rain, birds, insects and cats sun or groom themselves dry. The cold kinds play in falling snow, and the ones who love the sun and the heat shiver in it and go looking for cover. A friend following you stays with you whatever the sky.
message.harmontide.safety_line: %s holds you on her safety line: you float down unhurt.
message.harmontide.silk_bridge: %s spins a silk bridge %s blocks long. It will hold for a few minutes.
message.harmontide.silk_bridge_tired: %s is still spinning out the last bridge. Give her a moment.
message.harmontide.silk_bridge_none: %s looks for a gap in front of you to bridge, and finds none.
message.harmontide.carry_rest: %s needs to catch her breath before she can carry you again.
message.harmontide.carry_tiring: %s's wings are tiring. She will have to set you down soon.
message.harmontide.coiled: %s coils around you to shield you. Crouch to slip out.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.title: Getting about together
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal: Many kinds help you get about once they like you enough. A young jumping spider you are friends with hops onto your shoulder when you tell her to follow you, or when you crouch and hold out an empty hand. While she rides there, falls never hurt you and cobwebs no longer hold you. A gliderune rides there too, and slows your falls. Other tiny friends hop up when told to follow you: a fairy mends you a little, a pixie or a kesaran-pasaran brings luck, the waterlil cat lets you breathe under water, and the living doll lends you her night eyes. A harpy hatchling who likes you rides your shoulder like a parrot: crouch and hold out an empty hand. Crouch for two seconds to set any of them down. She stays down for a minute. Crouch and hand an arachne some string, and she spins a silk bridge across the gap in front of you. It lasts a few minutes. Do it while looking up at a wall and she strings a silk ladder up it instead. An arachne following you swings across on a silk line when she cannot walk to you. Saddle a tarantula, a wolf spider or an ushi-oni who trusts you a lot and ride her: she climbs straight up walls and cliffs with you on her back. A harpy who trusts you a lot lifts you when you crouch and hold out an empty hand. The big birds, such as rocs, albatrosses, swans and owls, fly you wherever you look for half a minute. Most others can only glide you down, and hummingbirds and finches are too small. When she tires she sets you down, and if you let go you drift down slowly. She also catches you if you fall past her. Ducks and swans float and paddle about ponds. Take hold of one while you both swim and she tows you. A mermaid takes your hand in the water and swims you anywhere you look, even far down, and you never run out of air. A lamia who trusts you a lot coils around you when you are badly hurt near her: you take less damage and heal, and your attackers turn on her. Land on a slime girl and you bounce back up unharmed. Crouch to sink in instead. Sit in a minecart on a track while a centaur follows you, and she takes the front and pulls you along. In the water, a capybara, turtle, water buffalo, hippo, beaver, polar bear or spinosaur friend lets you climb onto her back, and she swims you wherever you face. An octopus, a squid girl, a kraken, a cuttlefish or a nautilus dives with you instead, wherever you look, and shares her air. A mermaid who trusts you a lot swims ahead of your boat and pushes it along. Crouch and hold out an empty hand to a big construct friend, a golem, a talosling, an automaton or a gargoyle: she tosses you up and forward, and you land unhurt. Press jump again in mid-air and a friend with you may lift you once more: a kitsune following you gives a spirit leap, a sylph, angel or valkyrie a gust that lets you down gently, a wolpertinger a second hop, and a fairy or pixie on your shoulder a little flutter. Friends following you lend you a little of themselves: with a cat girl at your heels falls hurt half as much, a jackalope or a kangaroo puts a spring in your step, and a wolf or a hellhound sets the pack's pace when you sprint.
message.harmontide.crab_shed: %s has shed her shell. She gives you a piece of it.
message.harmontide.forest_given: %s tucks away %s %s. She will plant them around here.
message.harmontide.forest_done: %s has planted every sapling you gave her.
message.harmontide.shambler_company: With %s beside you, the dead take you for one of their own.
journal.harmontide.guide.jobs.title: Work about the home
journal.harmontide.guide.jobs: Girls who are fond of you lend a hand with the blocks around a home. A dragon walks over to a furnace, blast furnace or smoker that has something to cook in it and breathes on it: it burns without fuel and cooks twice as fast while she stays. The water dragons cannot do this. Cattle minotaurs and holstaurs carry buckets of milk from a chest or barrel to a cheese shelf with room on it. They take the hard cheeses off the shelves and put them in a chest that already holds cheese. Bug girls take the honey from full hives without angering the bees, and calm bees that are angry. The honey goes into a glass bottle if a chest nearby has one, else it comes as honeycomb. Fairies keep to their fountains instead. Hand a rodent a stack of saplings and she plants them all around the spot where you gave them to her, a few blocks apart. Hand a beaver an axe and she fells the wild trees around that spot, one every few minutes, and puts the logs into the nearest chest. She leaves anything built alone. Crouch with an empty hand to take the axe back. The mooskuh fills the bowls in a chest near her with mushroom stew, one every couple of minutes. A holstaur bakes a cake, with her own milk in it, from the sugar, egg and wheat in a chest beside a crafting table. A brownie or a domovoi bakes bread from the wheat there. A slime girl fills an empty cauldron near her with what she is made of, once every five minutes: the undine with water, the frost slime with powder snow, the magma slime with lava. A befriended crab sheds her shell every few days and gives you a piece. At a smithing table, a crab armour piece next to any worn tool, weapon or armour mends half its wear. No template is needed. While a zombie girl walks with you, the undead and creepers take you for one of their own and leave you alone, until you hit one. Girls do this work while they are free or on patrol, not while they follow you or sit.
message.harmontide.labyrinth: %1$s points %3$s. Home is %2$s blocks that way.
message.harmontide.labyrinth_below: %1$s points %3$s and down. Home is %2$s blocks that way, %4$s below you.
message.harmontide.labyrinth_above: %1$s points %3$s and up. Home is %2$s blocks that way, %4$s above you.
message.harmontide.labyrinth_here: %1$s stamps a hoof. You are home already.
journal.harmontide.guide.instincts.title: Little instincts
journal.harmontide.guide.instincts: Every kind has her own small ways. A minotaur never loses her way: show a minotaur friend a compass and she points the way home, to your bed or else the world's spawn, and tells you how far. At dusk a cat girl sometimes tears about for a few seconds for no reason at all. An owl harpy at your side in the dark lends you her eyes, and you see as if by day. On ice a penguin drops onto her belly and slides along three times as fast. A befriended boar girl roots about in soft ground now and then and turns something up: mushrooms, potatoes, carrots, beetroot seeds, and once in a while the seeds only a sniffer finds. A befriended anteater snaps up the silverfish near her, and a puff of dust shows you which stone around her is infested. A befriended giraffe browses the treetops and now and then shakes down an apple, a cocoa bean or a stick. A gryphon or a wyrm who would let you ride her catches you on her back if you fall past her. Now the other great fliers carry a devoted friend too: the wyvern, the long dragon, the amphiptere, Quetzalcoatl, Bahamut, the chimera, the ender dragon, the kun and the alebrije. When you are badly hurt, a kitsune who trusts you a lot wraps you in an illusion: you vanish for a few seconds and whatever was after you loses you. A mummy friend binds your wounds when you are down to half your health, and you heal quickly for a while. Lost underground? Show a bat girl friend a torch and she tells you which way the open sky is. Show a kitsune friend a lantern and she tells you the way to the nearest village. A dwarf shown one tells you the way to the nearest mineshaft.
message.harmontide.dwarf_anvil: %s knows this work: she gives you %s levels back.
message.harmontide.dinner_bell: %s friends come running at the bell.
message.harmontide.winged_catch: %s catches you before you hit the ground.
journal.harmontide.guide.workshop.title: Hands at the workbench
journal.harmontide.guide.workshop: Some kinds know their way round your workshop. An elf who is fond of anyone, standing near an enchanting table, knows what the bookshelves would tell it: the table offers enchantments as if fifteen stood around it. A smith friend at your side, a dwarf, a cyclops, an iron kobold or an anvil tortoise, gives back half the levels an anvil job cost you. A lich, or Koschei, keeps a brewing stand with potions and an ingredient in it going without blaze powder, and it brews twice as fast. A dragon lights an unlit campfire as well as tending furnaces. Ring a bell and your friends nearby who are free to come hurry over to it. A winged friend, such as a valkyrie, an angel, a sylph, a phantom or a moth girl, catches you before you hit the ground. Crouch and hand a plant girl friend bone meal while you look up at a wall, and she grows real vines up it for you to climb. A yuki-onna friend near you freezes the water under your feet as you walk across it. A fire kind friend near you, a salamander, a blaze cat, a magma slime, an ifrit, a fire giant or a hellhound, cools the lava under your feet into a crust you can walk on. It melts back a few seconds later. An arachne weaves the string in a chest beside a loom into white wool, four string to a block. A wood or desert elf turns flint, sticks and feathers in a chest beside a fletching table into arrows, four at a time. A sea snake or sea serpent lamia keeps you in her coils under the water too: she dives wherever you look, and you never run out of air.
