tip.harmontide.compass: Show it to a minotaur friend: she points the way home
tip.harmontide.sapling: Hand a stack to a rodent friend: she plants them
tip.harmontide.crab_armour_piece: Mends half a worn item's wear at a smithing table, no template
tip.harmontide.bell: Ring it to call your friends nearby
advancement.harmontide.shoulder_friend.d: Have a little friend ride on your shoulder
advancement.harmontide.carried_aloft.des: Be carried through the air by a harpy
advancement.harmontide.caught_falling.de: Be caught by a winged friend while falling
advancement.harmontide.ferried.desc: Be towed or carried across the water by a friend
advancement.harmontide.silk_bridge.desc: Have an arachne spin you a bridge across a gap
message.harmontide.fox_veil: %s wraps you in an illusion. For a moment, nothing can see you.
message.harmontide.bat_way_out: %1$s squeaks: the open sky is %2$s blocks %3$s, %4$s above you.
message.harmontide.bat_sky: %s flutters about you. You are under the open sky already.
message.harmontide.bat_lost: %s listens to the echoes and shakes her head. No way out near here.
message.harmontide.guide_way.village: %1$s points %3$s. The nearest village is about %2$s blocks that way.
message.harmontide.guide_way.mineshaft: %1$s points %3$s. An old mineshaft runs about %2$s blocks that way.
message.harmontide.guide_none.village: %s sniffs the wind and finds no village anywhere near.
message.harmontide.guide_none.mineshaft: %s taps the stone and hears no mineshaft anywhere near.
message.harmontide.guide_rest: %s is still getting her bearings. Ask her again in a moment.
tip.harmontide.lantern: Show it to a kitsune or dwarf friend: she knows the way
tip.harmontide.torch: Show it to a bat friend underground: she knows the way out
message.harmontide.beaver_axe: %s takes the axe. She will fell the wild trees around here and put the logs in the nearest chest.
advancement.harmontide.air_step.desc: Jump again in mid-air with a friend's help
message.harmontide.silk_ladder: %s strings a silk ladder %s blocks up the wall. It will hold for a few minutes.
message.harmontide.silk_ladder_none: %s looks for a wall in front of you to climb, and finds none.
message.harmontide.vine_ladder: %s coaxes vines %s blocks up the wall.
message.harmontide.vine_ladder_none: %s looks for a wall in front of you to grow vines on, and finds none.
tip.harmontide.bone_meal: Crouch and hand it to a plant girl friend, looking up a wall: vines to climb
journal.harmontide.guide.friends.p1: Feed her what she likes and pat her with an empty hand. At 10 friendship she is your friend: her gift of a behaviour starts, and a stick gives her orders (sneak for her stance).
journal.harmontide.guide.friends.p2: A harpy or centaur friend living near a mailbox of yours carries what you put in it: to the mailbox it's linked to (a feather on one, then on the other), or, unlinked, to you wherever you are.
journal.harmontide.guide.hearth.p1: A campfire ringed by eight stone bricks. Your friends roaming free within 16 blocks settle there; a day later each builds a hut nearby. With three or more, every morning they leave presents in the hearth.
journal.harmontide.guide.hearth.p2: With three living there a hearth becomes a hamlet: it takes a name (a name tag on the hearth changes it) and flies its own banner. With six it is a village, and now and then a wandering girl of a family new to it comes and asks to stay.
journal.harmontide.guide.hearth.p3: Word of your great deeds (the dragon slain, a village saved, a villager cured...) reaches home: come back to your hearth and your friends throw you a party.
journal.harmontide.guide.expedition.p1: Give a grown friend an empty map: she sets off and comes back a day later with finds of her homeland, and now and then a new friend.
journal.harmontide.guide.expedition.p2: Now and then she brings back a map she drew on the way, a red cross over a place nobody has explored yet: a chapel, a manor, the spire, an aerie or a grotto (the sea's girls chart grottoes, the realm's own its manors and spires;
journal.harmontide.guide.expedition.p3: scouts bring maps twice as often).
journal.harmontide.guide.home.p1: Brush her, throw her a ball, cook in a pot over a fire, spread a picnic blanket, share a soaking tub, set up a sparring post, a mirror and a gift box. A whistle calls everyone; a friend compass finds them.
journal.harmontide.guide.home.p2: Out in cold and mountain country there are hot springs: pools floored with geyserite that steam and never freeze.
journal.harmontide.guide.home.p3: A soak heals and warms you (a long one leaves you well soaked), your friends come and join you, and it cures a girl's cold. Lay geyserite under a pool at home (four calcite and a magma block make four) for an onsen of your own.
journal.harmontide.guide.home.p4: Every girl has a hobby of her own (gardening, fishing, reading, music, baking, collecting or knitting; her friends see it) and an hour of the day for it.
journal.harmontide.guide.home.p5: If a friend is about she leaves what she made at her feet: a gardener tends the crops round her, a reader shares what she learned, a musician's tune quickens everyone's work.
journal.harmontide.guide.home.p6: Keep her company through it and she shows you how, once a day.
journal.harmontide.guide.keepsakes.p1: A sketchbook draws a friend as a figurine for your shelf. A bedroll makes camp on the road. Every thirty days of close friendship she remembers, with presents.
journal.harmontide.guide.keepsakes.p2: A close friend who wears your bracelet forgives a long absence more easily; a love letter gets one back; share an umbrella in the rain.
journal.harmontide.guide.keepsakes.p3: Hold a flower in your other hand and open this journal to press it between the pages; it remembers the friend who was with you, and friends who know bring kinds you lack.
journal.harmontide.guide.dairy.p1: Pour milk into a butter churn and work it, by hand or with redstone. Set it on a cheese shelf underground: it firms in a day and hardens in three, stronger each time.
journal.harmontide.guide.dairy.p2: A fridge feeds the household; berries, honey, fish and the like flavour a friend's milk for a day, and so does food from your hand.
journal.harmontide.guide.nursing.p1: A mother with milk nurses her baby every few minutes. Feed the baby by hand to wean her; never weaned, her mother keeps her milk for good. Mothers foster orphans of any kind. Poisoned or withering under a roof?
journal.harmontide.guide.nursing.p2: A friend with milk brings you a cup. A cradle (planks around wool, on two sticks) helps too: at night the little ones nap beside it and grow twice as fast, and rocking it hums them a lullaby.
journal.harmontide.guide.nursing.p3: Be near as she grows: her first word, a flower she picked and a drawing of you both are moments she saves for you.
journal.harmontide.guide.encounters.p1: Now and then you meet one in trouble: caught in a web, chased by zombies, or lost in the rain. Cut the web, fight off the chasers, or lead her under a roof, and she won't forget it. One found hurt mends with a healing balm.
journal.harmontide.guide.encounters.p2: Every eight days, in the morning, a flock of wild harpies passing through comes down near you to rest: waterfowl by water, songbirds inland. They fly on the next day, all but any who has made a friend.
journal.harmontide.guide.encounters.p3: On the floor of warm seas lie merfolk grottoes: domes of prismarine and coral round a sunken chest, where a mermaid queen holds court with three of the reef's girls. Befriend the queen and her court takes you in.
journal.harmontide.guide.encounters.p4: (/harmontide locate grotto) Walk the beaches by day and now and then a bottle washes up: a map a girl drew, a little wreck treasure, or a letter from a lonely girl of the sea, who comes to meet whoever read it.
journal.harmontide.guide.encounters.p5: In cherry groves, bamboo jungles and birch woods, a path under red torii leads to a kitsune shrine and its shrine maiden. Leave a little food in the offering box and draw a fortune, once a day.
journal.harmontide.guide.encounters.p6: (/harmontide locate shrine) Under savannas, plains and deserts, a ring of mossy stone marks the way down into a Minoan labyrinth: a maze that's never the same twice, with a treasure at its heart and a minotaur who guards it.
journal.harmontide.guide.encounters.p7: (/harmontide locate labyrinth) Further afield: an oasis in the desert where a sphinx keeps an old shrine (and her riddles), sky islands drifting high over the hills where a sylph lives, and in dark forests a jorogumo's silk den,
journal.harmontide.guide.encounters.p8: its chest full of cocoons to tear open. (/harmontide locate oasis, island, den) Up in the mountains a dragon sleeps in her lair on a glittering hoard; out on the plains a centaur band keeps camp round a fire;
journal.harmontide.guide.encounters.p9: and in an old graveyard a yurei drifts among the headstones. (/harmontide locate lair, camp, graveyard)
journal.harmontide.guide.chores.p1: A friend you leave on patrol keeps the place: she gathers eggs, feathers and wool, takes the honey from full hives without upsetting the bees (put glass bottles in a chest for honey bottles), shears sheep,
journal.harmontide.guide.chores.p2: lights the dark corners with torches from a chest (so nothing spawns there), picks ripe sweet berries and glow berries, and fishes from the shore when there is nothing else to do.
journal.harmontide.guide.chores.p3: Plant girls and bugs on patrol tend the crops around their post too, a stage at a time. Food goes in a fridge nearby, the rest in a chest.
journal.harmontide.guide.festivals.p1: Every 24 days come four festivals: the Midsummer Dance on the 8th day, the Harvest Feast on the 16th, the Day of Hearts on the 20th and the Gift Exchange on the 24th. At dusk the girls who live at your hearth gather round it.
journal.harmontide.guide.festivals.p2: Join them: play a jukebox for the dance, stock a fridge for the feast, set out a cake for the Day of Hearts, and come empty-handed for the presents.
journal.harmontide.guide.market.p1: Every 6 days (the 4th, 10th, 16th and 22nd of the 24), if you are home that morning, a travelling girl from a family that doesn't live at your hearth sets up beside it, most often a kind you have never met.
journal.harmontide.guide.market.p2: Hand her an emerald for a bundle of her country's finds; she has four to sell. She moves on the next day, unless you have made a friend of her.
journal.harmontide.guide.market.p3: Once your hearth is a village, set a market stall within 16 blocks of it (a red and white awning over sticks, planks and a chest).
journal.harmontide.guide.market.p4: Every morning the passing trade buys half of what's on it, four items to the emerald, and each resident lays out something new: a farmhand her crops, a cook her baking, a guard arrows,
journal.harmontide.guide.market.p5: anyone else the kind of present she'd bring you. Out on the plains and meadows stand wayside inns, kept by a holstaur. Every morning a traveller or two from far away stops over for the day: make a friend of one and she stays.
journal.harmontide.guide.market.p6: An emerald to the innkeeper buys a hot meal, and sometimes a map a traveller left behind. (/harmontide locate inn)
journal.harmontide.guide.rivals.p1: Some wild kinds can't stand each other, by their branch of the tree of life rather than their looks: cats, hyenas and mongooses with rodents, snakes with rodents and frogs, wolves and foxes with hares and rodents, spiders,
journal.harmontide.guide.rivals.p2: bats and frogs with insects, seals and bears with fish, and the mongoose and meerkat with snakes. When they meet, one glowers and the other runs. Nobody gets hurt, and once a girl is your friend she has better things to do.
journal.harmontide.guide.roles.p1: A daughter who grows up picks a calling from what she grew up around. Farmland makes a farmhand: crops grow faster where she tends them.
journal.harmontide.guide.roles.p2: A kitchen (furnace, smoker, campfire or fridge) makes a cook: now and then she cooks something raw in a fridge. A bell or an iron golem makes a guard, tougher and stronger.
journal.harmontide.guide.roles.p3: Otherwise she becomes a scout: her expeditions take half the time and bring more home. A grown daughter may take a shine to a villager (or give the villager a flower while she is near to introduce them).
journal.harmontide.guide.roles.p4: After three mornings near each other they are wed, and now and then a little one comes along: your grandchild, as devoted to you as her mother is. Two at most each.
journal.harmontide.guide.roles.p5: Toys tip the scales, one a day: a wooden hoe for a farmhand, a bowl for a cook, a wooden sword for a guard, a compass for a scout. Show a little one a written book to read it to all the little ones near.
journal.harmontide.guide.bestiary.p1: A kind you have only glimpsed gets just her name here. Watch her kind a while and her home and her moment fill in; watch longer, or befriend one, and you learn her ways. Fully study 25 kinds to be a naturalist.
journal.harmontide.guide.bestiary.p2: A spyglass helps: whoever is in its crosshair, up to 64 blocks off, is studied twice as fast.
journal.harmontide.guide.treats.p1: Every girl has a favourite treat from her homeland. She takes it even if it isn't what she usually eats, and it means three times as much.
journal.harmontide.guide.treats.p2: And every girl has a birthday on one of the 24 days of the calendar: bring a friend something to eat that day and she'll never forget it. Look at a friend to see her birthday.
journal.harmontide.guide.treats.p3: A girl who is expecting craves one food and tells you when you come near; bring it to her before her time and she has twins.
journal.harmontide.guide.treats.p4: On her birthday, light a candle on a cake near her: she comes to blow it out, and everyone there is the closer for her wish.
journal.harmontide.guide.games.p1: Crouch and touch a friend with an empty hand to play hide and seek: count to ten while she hides, then find her within three minutes. Daughters love it most. Hit a friend with a snowball and she'll throw them right back for a while.
journal.harmontide.guide.games.p2: Show a friend a banner while pointing at somewhere a little way off and she'll race you there (win, and she pays up).
journal.harmontide.guide.games.p3: Hand her a shovel and she'll bury one of her presents nearby under suspicious sand or gravel: she calls warmer and colder as you look, and a brush digs it out.
journal.harmontide.guide.games.p4: Crouch and show a friend a bow near a target block for an archery match: three arrows each, closer to the middle scores more.
journal.harmontide.guide.mining.p1: Diggers (dwarves, gnomes, kobolds, moles, ants, constructs and more; look for "Miner") will mine for you. Hand one a pickaxe, then show her what to look for: an ore, raw metal, an ingot, a gem, coal or stone.
journal.harmontide.guide.mining.p2: She digs in at her patrol spot (or where she stands) and comes back there with a stack, into a chest beside the spot or into your hands. Rare things take days and wear the pickaxe; Efficiency, Fortune and Unbreaking help.
journal.harmontide.guide.mining.p3: Crouch with an empty hand to take your pickaxe back. She leaves a laddered shaft beside the spot that goes deeper while she's down (natural ground only), and brings up any ore she struck on the way.
journal.harmontide.guide.foraging.p1: Gatherers (plants, rabbits, rodents, foxes, bugs, marsupials and centaurs; look for "Forager") will forage for you.
journal.harmontide.guide.foraging.p2: Crouch and show one something that grows wild: berries, mushrooms, tar-shrooms, apples, flowers, saplings, seeds, honeycomb.
journal.harmontide.guide.foraging.p3: She goes out and comes back to her patrol spot (or where she stood) with sixteen of it and your sample, into a chest beside the spot or into your hands. Berries take a few hours, rare seeds days.
journal.harmontide.guide.longing.p1: Close friends miss you when you are away, and longing adds to it even while you are near.
journal.harmontide.guide.longing.p2: Tar-shrooms (black mushrooms of swamps and dark forests; they spread in the dark) make grown friends nearby long for you a little at a time, and a salami fed to one makes her long a lot.
journal.harmontide.guide.longing.p3: Leave for a minute or more and come back: if she misses you, she cuddles up to you, and is more likely to come to bed and to have young that day.
journal.harmontide.guide.stargazing.p1: On a clear night, stand still under open sky and look up at the stars. After a while your friends nearby come and sit beside you to look up.
journal.harmontide.guide.stargazing.p2: Before long a shooting star crosses the sky (one a night): everyone beside you grows a little closer, and one of them whispers her wish, which tells you her favourite treat.
journal.harmontide.guide.stargazing.p3: Each star falls through a constellation you haven't seen yet: the journal's cover keeps count of all twelve. Now and then, on a clear night in cold country, the sky fills with an aurora.
journal.harmontide.guide.stargazing.p4: A frost-touched girl or two comes out under it (and goes at dawn, unless she's made a friend), and aurora shards fall to the snow: every girl loves to be given one.
journal.harmontide.guide.favours.p1: Now and then a grown friend near you asks you for something she needs: candles, string, paper, ingots, whatever her people use. Look at her to see what (it shows on her info).
journal.harmontide.guide.favours.p2: Bring it within three days, all at once or a few at a time, and hand it to her: she is glad of it, grows closer, and gives you a few emeralds. You only owe one favour at a time.
journal.harmontide.guide.stories.p1: At night, sit by a lit campfire with two or more friends around it. One of them will tell a story (one a night), most often of a kind of her own branch of the tree of life that you haven't met, else one from her own people: its page opens in your journal,
journal.harmontide.guide.stories.p2: with where it lives. Everyone listening grows a little closer.
journal.harmontide.guide.colds.p1: Leave a girl out in the rain or snow somewhere cold for a few minutes and she may catch a cold (sea folk, the undead, constructs and slimes never do). She sneezes and is a little slow for three days.
journal.harmontide.guide.colds.p2: Hand her mushroom stew, beetroot soup, rabbit stew or a honey bottle and she feels better at once, and is grateful to whoever looked after her.
journal.harmontide.guide.tree.p1: Every kind belongs to a branch of the tree of life: cats with hyenas and mongooses, whales with hippos, salamanders with frogs. A body can fool you (the hyena runs like a dog), her branch decides her milk.
journal.harmontide.guide.tree.p2: The pages after the guide keep count of each branch you have started; meet every kind on one branch to complete it and earn its charm (in your offhand it lends that branch's milk's first effect).
journal.harmontide.guide.tree.p3: Your first friend of a kind gets talked about: wild ones of her branch nearby start a little fond of you. When a branch is down to its last kind or two, a 'Still to meet' page tells you where they live (but not who they are).
journal.harmontide.guide.rain.p1: Cats of every kind hate getting wet: caught in the rain with nowhere to be, a feliform looks for a roof nearby and waits it out.
journal.harmontide.guide.rain.p2: Frogs, newts and salamanders love it, and a friend of theirs who stands out in the rain with them grows a little closer (once a shower). Friends warn you a minute before it starts.
journal.harmontide.guide.rain.p3: Snakes, lizards, turtles and crocodiles are cold-blooded: on a clear morning they lie in the sun for a while and get up warmed through, and a friend who keeps them company there is a little closer.
journal.harmontide.guide.habits.p1: Each branch has its habits. Wolves, dogs and foxes howl at the full moon, and every canid in earshot answers; stand under the moon with a friend among them and you are closer for it.
journal.harmontide.guide.habits.p2: Monkeys and apes groom a friend beside them, picking out poison, hunger or the like now and then. Elephants and their kin spray a burning friend out.
journal.harmontide.guide.habits.p3: Walk beside a hoofed friend (cattle, goats, deer, camels, horses) and you find your footing the way she does, stepping up whole blocks without a jump. Bears, raccoons and their furry kin wrap up a friend who is freezing.
journal.harmontide.guide.habits.p4: Crabs, lobsters and shrimp comb the beach: stand on the sand by the water and one digs up something at your feet now and then.
journal.harmontide.guide.habits.p5: Fairies, pixies and the leshy leave fairy rings of mushrooms on the grass at night; stand in one (any ring of mushrooms will do) and you are lucky till morning.
journal.harmontide.guide.habits.p6: Hares and rabbits hear trouble first: one thumps the ground when a monster comes, and you learn what it is and which way. Fall beside a slime friend and you land on her, softly.
journal.harmontide.guide.habits.p7: With one of the made folk beside you, an anvil you work never wears down.
journal.harmontide.guide.nesting.p1: Build a nesting box (planks around a bit of wheat) and set it down where your hens are. Any egg laid within four blocks of it, by a chicken or a harpy, goes into the hay instead of rolling about.
journal.harmontide.guide.nesting.p2: Take the eggs out with an empty hand, or let a hopper do it; a friend on patrol nearby empties it into the fridge.
journal.harmontide.guide.nesting.p3: Up on the peaks, the windswept hills and the stony shores harpies keep aeries: crags topped with nests, one kind to a colony, led by a matriarch. Befriend her and the colony takes you in.
journal.harmontide.guide.nesting.p4: At home, a harpy perch (a hay bale and two feathers on spruce) draws a passing flock to settle round it for good. (/harmontide locate aerie)
journal.harmontide.guide.orders.p1: A stick gives a friend her orders: sit, patrol, follow or roam; sneak with it for her stance. Sneak with the whistle and everyone near stays put; do it again and they all follow you.
journal.harmontide.guide.orders.p2: Followers go through portals with you, take the free seat in your boat, and wait where they are while you are away. Sneak with the friend compass and the friends near you glow.
journal.harmontide.guide.orders.p3: Your arrows and blasts pass them by, and you hear it when one is badly hurt. The command /harmontide friends lists them all, wherever they are.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p1: Deep in some dark forests and swamps (where a little shrine of black stone and purple candles sometimes keeps the realm's gifts), and wherever a wild Lilith lives, the ground turns to purple Demon Realm grass,
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p2: and it creeps on by itself in the dark, a few steps past where it began, up into the trees, which weep violet sap; pale weepcaps glow among the roots, and the air turns heavy and rose-dark.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p3: Friends standing in it blush, miss you more and flirt more often. Its heartfruit bushes bear fruit: a close friend who eats one is lovestruck with you for a few minutes.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p4: Animals and monsters that linger on it in the dark change into monster girls of their kind: a witch into a succubus, a cow into a holstaur, an iron golem into a golem, a slime into a slime girl; a tamed pet stays devoted to you.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p5: Parrots become macaw harpies and frogs frog girls. Villagers, wandering traders, pigs, cats and chickens are possessed instead: they keep their own shape, but their eyes glow violet and the realm's haze rises from them,
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p6: and possessed animals seek out one of their own kind every half day, and their young are born piglettes, nekomata or poultry harpies.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p7: After a day possessed, the realm takes a pig, cat or chicken altogether the next time she is in the dark: she becomes a piglette, a nekomata or a poultry harpy herself.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p8: A possessed villager or wandering trader comes to a sleeping player's bed instead: one who spends the night there has a little succubus or demon a day later, devoted to that player.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p9: Give one a heartfruit and she seeks your bed that night from far off (and if she is slow, she slips in through the haze); and she speaks well of her young's father to the village.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p10: A possessed cat brings her owner a heartfruit each morning. Possessed animals follow a heartfruit held out to them, and one fed to any possessed creature makes her ready for her own kind at once.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p11: At night a possessed villager passes it on to a villager standing close by, so a village slowly turns. Little patches of the realm take root under them, and a golem among three of them turns too.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p12: Splash holy water (holy water and gunpowder), thrown, frees every possessed creature where it breaks.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p13: A holy font (calcite, holy water and gold) wards twelve blocks round it: the realm can't take hold there and nobody is possessed or turned.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p14: Now and then a wandering trader arrives already possessed, with a realm explorer map among her wares. Holy water drives it out of them.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p15: A holstaur fills a glass bottle with her milk, which makes you strong; baked into a heartfruit tart with heartfruit, wheat and sugar, it leaves a close friend lovestruck three times as long.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p16: Deep in the realm at night a wild succubus or demon sometimes steps out of the haze, and under a full moon the realm spreads fast and its own dance the sabbath.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p17: Changed ones still burn with the realm, and slip into any sleeper's bed, friend or not.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p18: A succubus near your bed visits your dreams: a close one brings a sweet dream and a lucky morning; a wild one feeds on some of your experience and leaves a heartfruit, unless a tapir guards your sleep.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p19: A realm censer (chain, iron, heartfruit and an amethyst shard) fed a heartfruit burns for a day, and the girls within eight blocks of it feel the realm's air without its ground: they flirt and miss you as if they stood in it.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p20: A realm log cut down and kept makes dark purple realm planks, stairs, slabs, fences, gates, doors and trapdoors that stay purple in any light.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p21: (/harmontide locate realm finds the nearest wild patch.) Realm silver (an iron ingot, four amethyst shards and a heartfruit) makes a sword that cuts the spirit, not the flesh: it wounds no monster girl,
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p22: but stops her fighting and leaves her blushing and a little fonder of you; anything else it cuts like iron.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p23: Realm silver armour guards like iron; two pieces soften a monster girl's blows by half, and a full set keeps wild ones from picking a fight.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p24: About one night in ten the moon rises rose-violet: that night the realm stirs, turning creatures twice as fast and spreading, possessing and calling its own four times as often.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p25: Torchlight turns it back to grass, and so does holy water (three bottles, a water bucket and a gold nugget). Silk touch takes the grass home.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p26: Deep in a few dark forests a Lilith keeps a manor of realm wood with her succubi, a throne, and the realm's treasures in a chest.
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p27: (/harmontide locate manor) In the badlands stands the Demon's spire: a blackstone tower of four storeys (a hall with succubi on guard, a library, a bedchamber, a treasury) and on its roof, under the open sky,
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p28: the Demon on her throne. (/harmontide locate spire) The realm takes on the land it spreads into: where it is cold enough to snow it is the frost realm, on mud and in swamps the bog realm (weepcaps thrive there, heartfruit does not),
journal.harmontide.guide.realm.p29: and on sand realm sand (heartfruit, but no weepcaps).
journal.harmontide.guide.order.p1: The Order is sworn to wipe out the Demon Realm. By day, now and then, a patrol of its sisters (two knights in white and gold, and an inquisitrix in a navy hood) marches on a realm patch near you to purge it: realm grass turns back where they walk,
journal.harmontide.guide.order.p2: and the inquisitrix blesses all of it around her. They free the possessed with a touch, and they put the realm's own to the sword: devils, and every girl the realm changed. Ordinary girls they leave alone.
journal.harmontide.guide.order.p3: The Order hears of your ties to the realm: time spent in its air, devils and changed girls among your friends, heartfruit handed out.
journal.harmontide.guide.order.p4: Once it has heard enough, you are marked: sisters fight you and the friends at your side, and patrols come looking for you.
journal.harmontide.guide.order.p5: When it has heard far too much, a crusade comes for your hearth one night: a captain under the Order's banner and her band.
journal.harmontide.guide.order.p6: Beat every one of them and your household is the fonder of you; if any still stand at dawn, they withdraw, and your household is shaken.
journal.harmontide.guide.order.p7: A realm silver blade cuts a sister's faith, not her flesh, and so does the realm's air in the dark: with no faith left she kneels and lays down her sword.
journal.harmontide.guide.order.p8: Feed a kneeling sister a heartfruit and she falls to the realm, a succubus (a captain a demon) devoted to you; with an empty hand you spare her, and she goes home.
journal.harmontide.guide.order.p9: A sister you spared remembers: a couple of days later, while the Order doesn't have you marked, she comes back to your hearth unarmed, as a chaplain, and stays three days.
journal.harmontide.guide.order.p10: Any wedding or vow renewal at a hearth while she is there gets her blessing. The Order thinks better of mercy and of exorcism. (/harmontide order tells you how the Order sees you.)
journal.harmontide.guide.kindred.p1: Keep company with the Demon Realm long enough and it takes to you. Time in its air, heartfruit you eat, nights beside one of its own, a wife of the realm's own at your side,
journal.harmontide.guide.kindred.p2: and sisters of the Order you bring to fall all leave its touch on you. Touched, you see in the realm's dark and its haze rises from you.
journal.harmontide.guide.kindred.p3: Kindred, its own know you: wild devils and realm-changed girls let you be unless you strike first, they are a little likelier to share your bed, and you move quickly in its air.
journal.harmontide.guide.kindred.p4: The Order counts it against you: a sister who sees you sprinkles holy water on you, and a chaplain won't bless your wedding.
journal.harmontide.guide.kindred.p5: Realm-born, the realm feeds you while you stand in its air, its night makes you strong, and you are hardier everywhere (two more hearts). Splash holy water washes much of it out, and time near a holy font a little.
journal.harmontide.guide.kindred.p6: (/harmontide realm touch tells you how far it has gone.)
journal.harmontide.guide.season.p1: Each branch of the tree of life has three restless days in every forty, each at its own time. A grown friend in season stays close to you, blushes, flirts more and comes to bed more readily.
journal.harmontide.guide.season.p2: Cold calms her: a cold biome, or a snowball or ice handed to her, which settles her until next season. Your friends list says who is in season.
journal.harmontide.guide.marriage.p1: A wedding ring (a diamond on three gold ingots) given to a grown friend who adores you, at full friendship, is a proposal. Stand by a hearth together and the wedding is held: your friends nearby gather round.
journal.harmontide.guide.marriage.p2: A spouse forgives any absence, comes to bed more readily, and while she is near you have two more hearts (each spouse near adds two more, up to six).
journal.harmontide.guide.marriage.p3: Many spouses are one happy family: a wife nearby blesses each new proposal, the wives are bridesmaids, a pat for one warms the others, two or more in your bed make a family bed, and if one is lost the rest hold you close.
journal.harmontide.guide.marriage.p4: Guests bring wedding presents, and the first three days are a honeymoon. Wed by a lit realm censer instead and the Demon Realm keeps your vows. Propose at her kind of place (as on a date) and it's perfect.
journal.harmontide.guide.marriage.p5: Of a morning, a wife you pass packs you lunch, and one who shared your bed may have dreamt of a real place nearby: go there together. Use a plain painting on your hearth with the family gathered round for a portrait with their names.
journal.harmontide.guide.marriage.p6: A girl who adores you may not wait to be asked: after a lovely date she might hand you the ring herself.
journal.harmontide.guide.marriage.p7: Every forty days she wears her veil again; give her the ring by a hearth on the day and you renew your vows, with the friends gathered round, the bouquet and a second honeymoon.
journal.harmontide.guide.marriage.p8: At the wedding she names a place she has always wanted to see; take her there for a souvenir and a pack of what you found.
journal.harmontide.guide.marriage.p9: Before any ring, ask her out: sneak and give a close friend a flower, and she'll tell you her kind of place (lots of flowers, the water's edge, somewhere high with a view, or the open night sky). Take her there and stay together half a minute.
journal.harmontide.guide.family.p1: A girl who is expecting craves one food and tells you; bring it before her time for twins (a harpy lays a full clutch). When her time comes you hear of it wherever you are, and little ones born to you come with a name.
journal.harmontide.guide.family.p2: A cradle (planks around wool, on two sticks) lets them nap at night and grow twice as fast; rock it for a lullaby. Read them a written book.
journal.harmontide.guide.family.p3: Give a little one a toy each day: a wooden hoe, a bowl, a wooden sword or a compass tips what she grows up to be. Be near as she grows: her first word, a flower, a drawing. In a thunderstorm she runs to you.
journal.harmontide.guide.family.p4: Grown, she brings you the first thing of her calling. Use a plain painting on your hearth with the family round you for a portrait.
journal.harmontide.guide.family.p5: On Reunion Day (the 12th of every 24) your grown children who live away come home at dusk with their sweethearts and little ones, if you are by your hearth, and go back the next morning.
journal.harmontide.guide.family.p6: A grown daughter who settles at your hearth builds a house of her own a little way off, with a cradle and a bed for her sweetheart, who moves in once they are wed; visit it when it's done.
journal.harmontide.guide.family.p7: The journal lists them all and draws your family tree, wife by wife and generation by generation, and /harmontide family tells you where everyone is.
journal.harmontide.guide.liaison.p1: Place an exchange desk (paper, a book, paper over planks) in a village and a villager takes it as the exchange liaison. She issues homestay permits and sells clothes and keepsakes.
journal.harmontide.guide.liaison.p2: Carry a permit and iron golems leave your friends alone, and villagers who see you with a friend think better of you, so their prices drop.
journal.harmontide.guide.inspections.p1: Carry a homestay permit and keep a hearth with residents, and the exchange office sends an inspector every week (the first a few days after).
journal.harmontide.guide.inspections.p2: By day, while you are home, she walks up to the fire and looks the place over: a bed for each resident there, at least eight food put away in a fridge or chest, nobody hurt, residents fond of you, and no monsters about. Two points each.
journal.harmontide.guide.inspections.p3: Six or more pays an emerald a point; ten also makes you a hero of the villages for a day. Under six you only get a warning. Her written report says what to fix.
journal.harmontide.guide.courtship.p1: Some kinds take to a stranger in their own way. Fighters (lizard warriors, the old bull breeds, oni and giants, hellhounds and wolves, wyrms, valkyries, dark elves, lionesses) respect whoever beats them face to face:
journal.harmontide.guide.courtship.p2: bring one to half health in melee and she yields instead of falling. Arrows don't count. Spinners and the tigress snare someone they fancy and come to claim them: don't strike her, and she claims you.
journal.harmontide.guide.courtship.p3: House spirits (kikimora, brownie, domovoi) let themselves in by your hearth while you are home and keep it; after a few visits they stay fond of the house. Each works once per creature, and only before she is fond of you.
journal.harmontide.guide.care.p1: Some kinds need a little more from the home you share. A merfolk who lives at your hearth needs a pool: six or more blocks of still water within eight of the fire.
journal.harmontide.guide.care.p2: She lives in it and never dries out at home; without one she reminds you every day, and it sours her a little. Lamias are cold-blooded: in a cold land they slow to a crawl unless warmed by a winter coat, a fire or campfire close by, or a hot spring.
journal.harmontide.guide.care.p3: Harpies moult every few days and give their favourite a handful of feathers.
journal.harmontide.guide.trials.p1: A wild legend tests anyone who comes near before she counts them a friend. The great birds, the deep's giants and the great serpents ask for an offering: hand it to her.
journal.harmontide.guide.trials.p2: Dragons, hellhounds, giants and the riders want to be bested face to face: bring her to half health in melee and she yields. The night's own and the sacred beasts want a vigil: stay close by her from dusk to dawn. A trial lasts three days.
journal.harmontide.guide.trials.p3: Pass it and she is fond of you and gives her relic: the sky plume, tide pearl, serpent's eye, dragon scale or moon mirror, each with its own gift.
journal.harmontide.guide.pacts.p1: The four elemental spirits bind themselves to one they love. Crouch and hand an amethyst shard to a devoted salamander, undine, sylph or gnome, and her element goes with you everywhere. Fire: your blows set foes alight.
journal.harmontide.guide.pacts.p2: Water: water and rain heal you. Wind: you are light on your feet, and quick under the open sky. Earth: deep underground you dig fast and stand firm. One spirit of each element at a time; a shard again ends the pact, and it ends if she dies.
journal.harmontide.guide.headgear.p1: A friend devoted to you gives you something for your head, once: a kitsune a fox mask (luck follows you), a jackalope bunny ears (monsters hunting you glow), a devil a witch hat (half again from experience),
journal.harmontide.guide.headgear.p2: a flora girl a flower crown (bees spare you, and the sun heals you a little). Harpies' feathers make the winged cap, which you craft.
journal.harmontide.guide.merchants.p1: Now and then a girl you meet in the wild is a wandering merchant, sparkling green over her pack.
journal.harmontide.guide.merchants.p2: An empty hand opens her trades: the wares of her branch of the tree of life, milk and wool from the cattle, silk from the spinners, saplings from the flora, realm fruit from the devils, gold from the dragons. She buys bread for the road.
journal.harmontide.guide.merchants.p3: Each trade makes her a little fonder of you. After two days she moves on, unless someone has made a friend of her: then she stays.
journal.harmontide.guide.squad.p1: Up to four of your fighting friends can be your squad: crouch and use a goat horn on one to enlist her, and again to let her go.
journal.harmontide.guide.squad.p2: Blow the horn and every squad member within earshot comes running and goes for the monsters around you for two minutes. Whatever strikes you, the squad near you turns on.
journal.harmontide.guide.squad.p3: And when the Order brings a crusade to your hearth, your squad marches home to defend it.
journal.harmontide.guide.blessings.p1: In the old stories a monster girl changes the place she makes her married home. Each wife near your hearth brings it her kind's blessing, and two or three wives of the same blessing make it stronger.
journal.harmontide.guide.blessings.p2: Plant folk, fae, birds and the small grazers make the crops round the hearth grow. Hoofed and horned kinds make young animals grow up and parents ready sooner.
journal.harmontide.guide.blessings.p3: Sea, river and shore kinds bring you luck at home, so the fish bite better. Hunters, the made, riders and the dead mark and weaken monsters that come close. Dragons, serpents and spinners quicken your hands (Haste).
journal.harmontide.guide.blessings.p4: Devils and slimes close your wounds by the fire.
journal.harmontide.guide.dead_realm.p1: Where a wild lich or koschei makes her home, the ground turns to ashen grave grass and a grey mist hangs over it.
journal.harmontide.guide.dead_realm.p2: It spreads in the dark, under trees and roofs and at night, but the open sun withers it back to its heart by day, and lamplight, holy water and the Order's sisters cleanse it.
journal.harmontide.guide.dead_realm.p3: Zombies and skeletons that linger on it in the dark rise again as undead girls, and deep in it, at night, one of the dead sometimes climbs out of the ground. Undead friends standing on it are at their strongest.
journal.harmontide.guide.dead_realm.p4: Befriend its lich, and it stops growing.
journal.harmontide.guide.sabbath.p1: The witches' Sabbath is the Demon Realm's own coven, and the Order's oldest rival.
journal.harmontide.guide.sabbath.p2: Whatever the Order holds against you raises your standing with the Sabbath, and so does dancing at the full-moon sabbath, seeing a creature turned by the realm, and being wed by a realm censer.
journal.harmontide.guide.sabbath.p3: Tithes, mercy to the Order and holy water lower it. As an initiate, witches leave you alone. As an adept, a witch offered an empty hand opens her table: heartfruit, weepcaps, censers, realm grass and brews.
journal.harmontide.guide.sabbath.p4: A keeper is given a familiar, a black cat whose eyes you share at night; lose her and another comes at the next full moon. And the Sabbath's sibling carries its title after their name.
journal.harmontide.guide.sea.p1: Wed a merfolk or mollusk bride by a hearth with water beside it, and if another sea girl stands among the guests she officiates as the sea bishop.
journal.harmontide.guide.sea.p2: Her blessing lets you breathe the water of the sea, the beaches and the rivers and swim like a dolphin, for as long as you are wed.
journal.harmontide.guide.sea.p3: And once in your life a merfolk close friend may give you a vial of her blood when you pet her: drink it for a lasting extra heart.
journal.harmontide.guide.ghosts.p1: Ghosts (yurei, banshees, poltergeists, lost souls, lloronas) like to be close to the one they love, as close as can be.
journal.harmontide.guide.ghosts.p2: Crouch and offer a ghost friend an empty hand and she slips into you for a minute: you see in the dark, a faint glow hangs about you, and monsters lose track of you. Each can do it once a day.
journal.harmontide.guide.ghosts.p3: Wild ghosts sometimes do it at night as a prank, leaving you shivering and hiccuping.
journal.harmontide.guide.cooking.p1: Crouch and hand a friend something raw (meat, fish, a potato) and she cooks it for you, now and then.
journal.harmontide.guide.cooking.p2: Every girl has her own touch in the kitchen and it never changes: a masterful cook's dish fills you up and leaves you strong, a good cook's heals a little, and a plain cook's is just dinner.
journal.harmontide.guide.cooking.p3: And some can't cook at all: their burnt love food makes you queasy, but eat it anyway while she's near and she'll be over the moon.
journal.harmontide.guide.dullahan.p1: A dullahan's head sits on her neck more by habit than anything. Startle her (a blow, a tease that flusters her, a stumble) and it pops off and rolls away. Headless, she stumbles slowly after it.
journal.harmontide.guide.dullahan.p2: Catch it first and hand it back, and she'll be very grateful. Keep it, and it finds its own way home after a while.
journal.harmontide.guide.cursed.p1: Now and then the chests of old places (dungeons, mineshafts, strongholds, temples, mansions, ancient cities) hold cursed gear: a black blade or a living breastplate, each with a spirit in it.
journal.harmontide.guide.cursed.p2: They work as well as iron, and they grow fond of whoever uses them: the blade with every kill, the armour with every blow it takes for you and every minute you wear it. They whisper to you as they do.
journal.harmontide.guide.cursed.p3: At full fondness the spirit steps out as a girl, devoted to you from the first: the living armour shrugs off blows and goes for whatever hurts you, and the cursed blade's strikes heal her.
journal.harmontide.guide.repeadead.p1: In dark forests, swamps and the deep dark she stands or crouches stock-still, her mourning mask frozen in horror. Walk in front of her and she screams: you can't move while she comes for you and clings on, drinking your life.
journal.harmontide.guide.repeadead.p2: Hit her while she holds you to break free. Befriended, she leaves friendly creatures be and turns her scream and her grip on the monsters around you.
journal.harmontide.guide.foodweb.p1: Wild girls feed themselves as their diet says. Hunters bring down the wild animals of their size (rabbits and chickens for the small, sheep, pigs and goats for most, cows for the big ones), eat the meat where it fell and leave the bones and hide.
journal.harmontide.guide.foodweb.p2: Fishers take fish and squid. Grazers crop the grass and flowers, and where many graze together the turf wears to bare dirt. Scavengers go where something died and eat what was left.
journal.harmontide.guide.foodweb.p3: Where the land is eaten out they move on, and thinned-out herds come back over time when no hunter is about. Your animals are safe: nothing tame, named, leashed or penned, nothing in a village or near a hearth.
journal.harmontide.guide.foodweb.p4: Befriended girls are fed by you and don't hunt.
journal.harmontide.guide.carcasses.p1: A wild animal killed by anything but you (a hunter, a wolf, a monster, a fall) leaves a carcass where it fell, bloodied, with feathers or wool torn loose round it.
journal.harmontide.guide.carcasses.p2: Scavengers and hungry hunters come to feed on it, and each meal takes meat off the bones. A cow carries the most meat, a pig a little less, a sheep or goat half as much, a chicken or rabbit a mouthful.
journal.harmontide.guide.carcasses.p3: Use a sword or an axe on it to butcher it: a share of the meat that's left, the hide or wool, and a bone. After a day it starts to rot (flies, and some of the meat comes away rotten); after two only bones are left, and on the third day nothing.
journal.harmontide.guide.rhythms.p1: Every kind keeps its own hours. Most are up by day and sleep at night; night kinds sleep through the day. Dawn-and-dusk kinds are up at first and last light and rest through midday and the dead of night, and a few nap in short bouts round the clock.
journal.harmontide.guide.rhythms.p2: A wild girl out in the open looks for somewhere covered to sleep first: under trees, an overhang or a roof. Asleep she isn't foraging or watching for you, so that is the time to meet the shy ones.
journal.harmontide.guide.rhythms.p3: Look at any girl to see her place in the food web and her hours.
journal.harmontide.guide.herds.p1: Wild grazers keep together with their own kind, and wild fish-eaters swim together as a school, all heading the same way; a straggler hurries back. Each of them keeps watch.
journal.harmontide.guide.herds.p2: At a monster, a wild hunter of another kind, or a stranger running up (or walking right up), the first to see it calls the alarm.
journal.harmontide.guide.herds.p3: A big herd, or a herd of big kinds, bunches up and faces the danger, hard to hurt; a small one flees together, all the same way. Schools always flee. Sneak, and you can get close.
journal.harmontide.guide.pasture.p1: The land remembers where it was grazed. A herd of three or more that keeps walking the same ground treads the grass into a game trail; follow one and it leads to them. Where grazers crowd together the turf wears to bare dirt.
journal.harmontide.guide.pasture.p2: Once the herd has moved on, the land rests: cropped grass grows back within half a day (now and then a flower with it), bare dirt greens over in a day, and a trail fades back to grass in two.
journal.harmontide.guide.territories.p1: Wild hunters each hold a home range of their own. Now and then one patrols out to its edge and leaves a scent mark there.
journal.harmontide.guide.territories.p2: A rival of her kind who comes across a fresh mark turns away and makes her home somewhere else, so hunters spread out across the land instead of crowding together.
journal.harmontide.guide.territories.p3: You can't smell the marks yourself, but a befriended dog, cat, bear or snake kind can: with one near you, the marks round about show as faint wisps in the colour of whoever left them. Marks fade after two days unless they are renewed.
journal.harmontide.guide.pollination.p1: Bees, moths, butterflies, fairies, pixies and nectar bats go from flower to flower, wild or befriended, and carry pollen between them.
journal.harmontide.guide.pollination.p2: A flower they pollinate seeds another of its kind beside it, and the crops, stems and berry bushes round it grow on a little: keep a pollinator friend near your garden.
journal.harmontide.guide.pollination.p3: Wild girls who eat fruit, nuts and seeds carry a seed away from their meals and leave it far off on open grass: a sapling suited to the land, or a berry bush in the taiga. They never sow in villages or near a hearth.
journal.harmontide.guide.partners.p1: Some kinds do better together. Small crabs and shrimp groom the big sea girls (orcas, sharks, krakens) in the water, soothing them and earning a meal. A hermit crab shelters by a sea anemone and is hard to hurt there.
journal.harmontide.guide.partners.p2: Small rodents and rabbit kinds ride close by the big grazers (elephants, giraffes, rhinos), picking them clean and staying safe by them.
journal.harmontide.guide.partners.p3: Ants guard plant girls and go for any monster that comes near them, and pollinators at a plant girl's blossoms keep her thriving.
journal.harmontide.guide.partners.p4: Scavengers trail wild hunters at a distance to be near the kill, and grazers of different kinds heed each other's alarm calls. Partners work for you too: keep an ant friend by your alraune.
journal.harmontide.guide.decomposers.p1: Slimes, the fungus kinds (matango, shiitake, censhroom, shroomotaur, cordyceps) and the date beetle break down whatever is left lying about: rotten flesh, bones, spoiled food, leaves, saplings, seeds and flowers.
journal.harmontide.guide.decomposers.p2: They pick carcasses to the bone faster and break the last bones into bone meal. What they take in goes back to the soil: coarse dirt loosens, bare dirt greens over, crops and saplings round them get a dose of bone meal.
journal.harmontide.guide.decomposers.p3: Keep a decomposer friend by your composter and she fills it for you.
journal.harmontide.guide.habitats.p1: Every kind cares about the little things about where she is: shade or sun, water close by or dry ground, heights, caves, cold or heat. Look at a girl to see what she likes and how she feels where she is.
journal.harmontide.guide.habitats.p2: Content, she heals slowly and sparkles now and then; ill at ease, she sighs, and a wild one wanders off to find a spot that suits her better. They turn up most where the land suits them, so if you are looking for one, look where she would be comfortable.
journal.harmontide.guide.habitats.p3: Make a friend comfortable at home and she will thank you for it with her health.
journal.harmontide.guide.tracks.p1: Wild girls leave signs of where they have been. In sand, snow and mud they leave footprints, pointing the way they went: hooves, paws, three-toed claws, bare feet, or the long sweep of a tail.
journal.harmontide.guide.tracks.p2: Use an empty hand on footprints to read them: whose they are, how fresh, and which way she went. Every kind you read goes into your field notes. Footprints fade after a day.
journal.harmontide.guide.tracks.p3: Bird kinds drop a feather now and then, and the gnawers and antlered kinds strip the bark off logs where nobody took an axe.
journal.harmontide.guide.weather.p1: Every kind meets the weather in her own way. In a thunderstorm most take cover under trees, an overhang or a roof and huddle there till it passes; the raiju, the sylph and the dragons are thrilled by it instead,
journal.harmontide.guide.weather.p2: faster and stronger in the open. Frogs and newts, slimes, snails and the fungus kinds come out and liven up in the rain, even the ones who usually sleep through the day.
journal.harmontide.guide.weather.p3: When the sun comes back after rain, birds, insects and cats sun or groom themselves dry. The cold kinds play in falling snow, and the ones who love the sun and the heat shiver in it and go looking for cover.
journal.harmontide.guide.weather.p4: A friend following you stays with you whatever the sky.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p1: Many kinds help you get about once they like you enough. A young jumping spider you are friends with hops onto your shoulder when you tell her to follow you, or when you crouch and hold out an empty hand.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p2: While she rides there, falls never hurt you and cobwebs no longer hold you. A gliderune rides there too, and slows your falls.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p3: Other tiny friends hop up when told to follow you: a fairy mends you a little, a pixie or a kesaran-pasaran brings luck, the waterlil cat lets you breathe under water, and the living doll lends you her night eyes.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p4: A harpy hatchling who likes you rides your shoulder like a parrot: crouch and hold out an empty hand. Crouch for two seconds to set any of them down. She stays down for a minute.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p5: Crouch and hand an arachne some string, and she spins a silk bridge across the gap in front of you. It lasts a few minutes. Do it while looking up at a wall and she strings a silk ladder up it instead.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p6: An arachne following you swings across on a silk line when she cannot walk to you.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p7: Saddle a tarantula, a wolf spider or an ushi-oni who trusts you a lot and ride her: she climbs straight up walls and cliffs with you on her back.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p8: A harpy who trusts you a lot lifts you when you crouch and hold out an empty hand. The big birds, such as rocs, albatrosses, swans and owls, fly you wherever you look for half a minute.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p9: Most others can only glide you down, and hummingbirds and finches are too small. When she tires she sets you down, and if you let go you drift down slowly. She also catches you if you fall past her.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p10: Ducks and swans float and paddle about ponds. Take hold of one while you both swim and she tows you. A mermaid takes your hand in the water and swims you anywhere you look, even far down, and you never run out of air.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p11: A lamia who trusts you a lot coils around you when you are badly hurt near her: you take less damage and heal, and your attackers turn on her. Land on a slime girl and you bounce back up unharmed.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p12: Crouch to sink in instead. Sit in a minecart on a track while a centaur follows you, and she takes the front and pulls you along.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p13: In the water, a capybara, turtle, water buffalo, hippo, beaver, polar bear or spinosaur friend lets you climb onto her back, and she swims you wherever you face.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p14: An octopus, a squid girl, a kraken, a cuttlefish or a nautilus dives with you instead, wherever you look, and shares her air. A mermaid who trusts you a lot swims ahead of your boat and pushes it along.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p15: Crouch and hold out an empty hand to a big construct friend, a golem, a talosling, an automaton or a gargoyle: she tosses you up and forward, and you land unhurt.
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p16: Press jump again in mid-air and a friend with you may lift you once more: a kitsune following you gives a spirit leap, a sylph, angel or valkyrie a gust that lets you down gently, a wolpertinger a second hop,
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p17: and a fairy or pixie on your shoulder a little flutter. Friends following you lend you a little of themselves: with a cat girl at your heels falls hurt half as much, a jackalope or a kangaroo puts a spring in your step,
journal.harmontide.guide.traversal.p18: and a wolf or a hellhound sets the pack's pace when you sprint.
journal.harmontide.guide.jobs.p1: Girls who are fond of you lend a hand with the blocks around a home.
journal.harmontide.guide.jobs.p2: A dragon walks over to a furnace, blast furnace or smoker that has something to cook in it and breathes on it: it burns without fuel and cooks twice as fast while she stays. The water dragons cannot do this.
journal.harmontide.guide.jobs.p3: Cattle minotaurs and holstaurs carry buckets of milk from a chest or barrel to a cheese shelf with room on it. They take the hard cheeses off the shelves and put them in a chest that already holds cheese.
journal.harmontide.guide.jobs.p4: Bug girls take the honey from full hives without angering the bees, and calm bees that are angry. The honey goes into a glass bottle if a chest nearby has one, else it comes as honeycomb.
journal.harmontide.guide.jobs.p5: Fairies keep to their fountains instead. Hand a rodent a stack of saplings and she plants them all around the spot where you gave them to her, a few blocks apart.
journal.harmontide.guide.jobs.p6: Hand a beaver an axe and she fells the wild trees around that spot, one every few minutes, and puts the logs into the nearest chest. She leaves anything built alone. Crouch with an empty hand to take the axe back.
journal.harmontide.guide.jobs.p7: The mooskuh fills the bowls in a chest near her with mushroom stew, one every couple of minutes. A holstaur bakes a cake, with her own milk in it, from the sugar, egg and wheat in a chest beside a crafting table.
journal.harmontide.guide.jobs.p8: A brownie or a domovoi bakes bread from the wheat there. A slime girl fills an empty cauldron near her with what she is made of, once every five minutes: the undine with water, the frost slime with powder snow,
journal.harmontide.guide.jobs.p9: the magma slime with lava. A befriended crab sheds her shell every few days and gives you a piece. At a smithing table, a crab armour piece next to any worn tool, weapon or armour mends half its wear. No template is needed.
journal.harmontide.guide.jobs.p10: While a zombie girl walks with you, the undead and creepers take you for one of their own and leave you alone, until you hit one. Girls do this work while they are free or on patrol, not while they follow you or sit.
journal.harmontide.guide.instincts.p1: Every kind has her own small ways. A minotaur never loses her way: show a minotaur friend a compass and she points the way home, to your bed or else the world's spawn, and tells you how far.
journal.harmontide.guide.instincts.p2: At dusk a cat girl sometimes tears about for a few seconds for no reason at all. An owl harpy at your side in the dark lends you her eyes, and you see as if by day. On ice a penguin drops onto her belly and slides along three times as fast.
journal.harmontide.guide.instincts.p3: A befriended boar girl roots about in soft ground now and then and turns something up: mushrooms, potatoes, carrots, beetroot seeds, and once in a while the seeds only a sniffer finds.
journal.harmontide.guide.instincts.p4: A befriended anteater snaps up the silverfish near her, and a puff of dust shows you which stone around her is infested. A befriended giraffe browses the treetops and now and then shakes down an apple, a cocoa bean or a stick.
journal.harmontide.guide.instincts.p5: A gryphon or a wyrm who would let you ride her catches you on her back if you fall past her.
journal.harmontide.guide.instincts.p6: Now the other great fliers carry a devoted friend too: the wyvern, the long dragon, the amphiptere, Quetzalcoatl, Bahamut, the chimera, the ender dragon, the kun and the alebrije.
journal.harmontide.guide.instincts.p7: When you are badly hurt, a kitsune who trusts you a lot wraps you in an illusion: you vanish for a few seconds and whatever was after you loses you.
journal.harmontide.guide.instincts.p8: A mummy friend binds your wounds when you are down to half your health, and you heal quickly for a while. Lost underground? Show a bat girl friend a torch and she tells you which way the open sky is.
journal.harmontide.guide.instincts.p9: Show a kitsune friend a lantern and she tells you the way to the nearest village. A dwarf shown one tells you the way to the nearest mineshaft.
journal.harmontide.guide.workshop.p1: Some kinds know their way round your workshop. An elf who is fond of anyone, standing near an enchanting table, knows what the bookshelves would tell it:
journal.harmontide.guide.workshop.p2: the table offers enchantments as if fifteen stood around it. A smith friend at your side, a dwarf, a cyclops, an iron kobold or an anvil tortoise, gives back half the levels an anvil job cost you.
journal.harmontide.guide.workshop.p3: A lich, or Koschei, keeps a brewing stand with potions and an ingredient in it going without blaze powder, and it brews twice as fast. A dragon lights an unlit campfire as well as tending furnaces.
journal.harmontide.guide.workshop.p4: Ring a bell and your friends nearby who are free to come hurry over to it. A winged friend, such as a valkyrie, an angel, a sylph, a phantom or a moth girl, catches you before you hit the ground.
journal.harmontide.guide.workshop.p5: Crouch and hand a plant girl friend bone meal while you look up at a wall, and she grows real vines up it for you to climb. A yuki-onna friend near you freezes the water under your feet as you walk across it.
journal.harmontide.guide.workshop.p6: A fire kind friend near you, a salamander, a blaze cat, a magma slime, an ifrit, a fire giant or a hellhound, cools the lava under your feet into a crust you can walk on. It melts back a few seconds later.
journal.harmontide.guide.workshop.p7: An arachne weaves the string in a chest beside a loom into white wool, four string to a block. A wood or desert elf turns flint, sticks and feathers in a chest beside a fletching table into arrows, four at a time.
journal.harmontide.guide.workshop.p8: A sea snake or sea serpent lamia keeps you in her coils under the water too: she dives wherever you look, and you never run out of air.
journal.harmontide.tiger_nekomata.signat: Ambush, fishing & roar: Crouched in bamboo or tall grass she is nearly invisible until she pounces (a strong opening strike). She catches fish in rivers and brings them to her favourites.
Her roar makes hostile mobs within 12 blocks flee for a few seconds.
journal.harmontide.snow_leopard_nekomata: Cliff leaps & warm tail: She jumps across gaps up to six blocks and never takes fall damage.
A bonded snow leopard near you stops you freezing in powder snow; asleep beside you she wraps you in her tail (no freezing, Resistance I when you wake).
journal.harmontide.lynx_nekomata.signatu: Snowshoe paws & rabbit hunter: She never sinks into powder snow and moves at full speed on snow. She keeps rabbits away from your crops and brings you rabbit hide and rabbit's feet.
Watched for too long, she slips out of sight (she breaks line of sight and hides).
journal.harmontide.cobra_lamia.signature: Hood & snake charming: The hood display is a warning: back off and nothing happens; come closer and she spits venom (Blindness and Poison).
A jukebox within 16 blocks keeps her calm, and a bonded cobra sways to it (the existing music system).
journal.harmontide.orb_weaver_arachne.si: Hunting web and phantom net: Wild, she strings cobwebs round the spot she settled on and goes for whatever they catch (players included) until fed meat.
Bonded, she spins a web at night by your bed instead; phantoms, bats and vexes are caught in it. It fades at dawn.
journal.harmontide.unicorn_centaur.signa: Pure heart, healing horn: A player who has killed villagers or iron golems can never befriend her, and she keeps away from them. Her horn clears poison and wither from friends near her and speeds up the cure of zombie villagers.
journal.harmontide.koi_mermaid.signature: Good fortune & waterfall climb: A bonded koi in a pond within 32 blocks of you gives Luck (better fishing and loot). She swims up water columns.
Ten days at full devotion turns her into a dragon koi (a golden glow mask and longer fins).
journal.harmontide.snapping_turtle_lizar: Tongue lure: While she sits still in water she catches a fish now and then and drops it at her feet (cod or salmon, at most three lying around at a time). Hit her and she hides in her shell.
Her bite is the hardest in the family after the crocodile's.
journal.harmontide.anubis_canid.signatur: The weighing: She weighs every player who comes near. Anyone who killed villagers or iron golems is condemned and hunted. Others may open the tomb chests she guards.
Each villager you cure and each iron golem you build lightens a heavy heart by one; when your deeds balance your deaths, show her a feather to be weighed again.
